plan.KONU:
EVALUATION
Sub-themes: "Body parts, human illnesses and diseases; human nature and human well-being today and in the future; fashion and personal fashion preferences''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Vocabulary for body parts
Nouns: A forehead, an eyebrow, an eyelash, a chin, a chest, lips, a tongue. Vocabulary for human illnesses and diseases:
Nouns: A cold, flu, a fever, a cough, a headache, a stomach ache, a sore throat, a toothache, a backache, an earache, an allergy, an allergic reaction, diabetes, COVID, acne, malaria, chickenpox, measles, a painkiller, an emergency. Verbs: To vomit, to feel dizzy, to breathe.
Adjectives: Painful.
Vocabulary for human nature and human well-being today and in the future:
Nouns: Empathy, social connection, happiness, global citizenship, digital detox, sustainability, self-care. Adjectives: Ambitious, compassionate, courageous.
Vocabulary for fashion and personal fashion preferences
Nouns: (Accessories): A scarf, a headscarf, a necklace, earrings, a bracelet, a ring, a watch, a belt, a hat, a handbag, a hairband (a headband-AmE), a cap, a benie, a tie, a bow tie, gloves, a backpack (rucksack). Adjectives: (Styles): Stylish, trendy, classy, smart casual, vintage, neat, well-dressed, (Clothing materials): denim, leather, cotton. (Clothing patterns): floral, striped, plain, checked, patterned.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, "Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)", "Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)".
*
(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
All future tenses mixed: (revisional): (By next year, she will have improved her health by running every day. She is going to start yoga this weekend to improve flexibility and balance. I will try to stay resilient no matter how difficult things get in the future.)
-
Can for ability (revisional): (I can lift heavy weights with my arms because I work out every day.)
-
Comparative Adjectives (Regular, Irregular) (revisional): (His new haircut looks better than his previous style. She is more ambitious than anyone in her social circle.)
-
The Simple Present vs Present Progressive for Future: (She exercises every morning to keep fit and healthy. She is exercising at the gym right now to stay fit.)
-
Should for Advice: (You should wear a scarf in winter to protect your neck from cold winds.)
-
Could for ability: (She could run a marathon if she trains her legs and increases her endurance.)
-
Adjectives (regular, -ing ending, -ed ending): (She has a beautiful face with sparkling eyes. The patient felt dizzy after experiencing a high fever. Her amazing energy inspires everyone in her fashion design team. After running for an hour, he felt exhausted and his legs were sore).
-
As…as, same…as, like, alike: (My sister’s hair is as long as mine, both silky and healthy. Her style is similar to a vintage fashion icon, effortlessly chic.)
Functions of the Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Use of the Simple Present vs. the Present Progressive for Future: Expressing scheduled or timetabled future events (Simple Present); expressing current intentions, ongoing plans, or arrangements for the near future. (Present Progressive).
Use of All Future Tenses (Mixed) (revisional): Expressing various degrees of certainty, intention, probability, and aspirations about future actions, events, and plans.
-
Use of modal “Should” for Advice: Giving suggestions, advice, and recommendations about what is right or appropriate.
-
Use of modal “Can” for Ability: Expressing past abilities, hypothetical situations, and future possibilities.
-
Use of modal “Could” for Ability: Expressing present or future abilities, skills or possibilities.
-
Use of Adjectives (Regular, -ing ending, -ed ending): Describing characteristics, emotions, and states (regular adjectives); describing ongoing actions or experiences (adjectives with -ing endings); describing feelings or states resulting from experiences (adjectives with -ed endings).
-
Use of Comparative Adjectives (Regular, Irregular): Comparing two things in terms of greater or lesser degree.
-
Use of “As…as, Same…as, Like, Alike”: Expressing similarity, comparison, and likeness between objects, actions, or people; describing similarities in personal habits.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
At last, you’re here in the flesh!
Let’s break the leg for the concert tonight! Oh, my God! I’m in her bad books!
My grandpa is fit as a fiddle despite his age! I’m feeling in the pink and ready to study!
Target Phonetical Sounds in Use
Vowels: e: (/e/; /i:/, /ə/)
Consonants: f: (/f/), g: (/g/, /dʒ/), h: (/h/)
*
(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme.)

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students create a project titled ''Personal Life and Well-Being'' focusing on the body parts, human illnesses and diseases; human nature and well-being today and in the future; and fashion and personal preferences. Students begin by exploring the human body and describing key body parts and their functions. They then discuss common illnesses and diseases, including ways to stay healthy and prevent these conditions according to their ages and levels. Then, students reflect on human well-being, comparing how people maintain physical and mental health today versus what it might look like in the future. Finally, students explore the role of fashion in personal identity by describing their fashion preferences and how clothing choices affect confidence and self-expression. The project can include written descriptions, illustrations, or creative presentations, such as posters or digital slideshows. Students will present their findings in class. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.
EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
Expansion
Objective: To talk about human nature and human well-being today and in the future; fashion and personal fashion preferences in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity 1: Future Well-being Plan
Students individually create a future lifestyle plan that focuses on personal health, fashion preferences, and sustainability, including details about diet, exercise, digital habits, and fashion choices. For example, a student might write, ''In 2030, I will exercise five times a week to stay healthy and choose sustainable, cotton-based clothing to protect the environment''. After preparing their plans, students present them in small groups, comparing their ideas using sentences such as, ''This plan is more suitable (sustainable) than my current lifestyle'', or ''It will be as trendy as fast fashion but more eco-friendly''. In the end, the teacher gives feedback on pronunciation, the use of target vocabulary, and target grammar. The students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
Supporting
Objective: To talk about human illnesses, diseases and give advice in English through a role play activity by using the target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Doctor & Patient Role-Play
Students work in pairs with predetermined roles: Student A as the ''Doctor'' and Student B as the ''Patient''. The teacher prepares papers with symptoms and related advice (e.g., ''headache—take a painkiller'') and places them in a box. Each pair selects a paper. The ''Patient'' uses the symptom to explain their problem (e.g., ''I have a headache''), and the ''Doctor'' gives advice based on the paper (e.g., ''You should take a painkiller''). After each pair performs, the teacher and other students provide constructive and supportive feedback on pronunciation and sentence accuracy. The students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

plan.KONU:
Sub-themes: "Body parts, human illnesses and diseases; human nature and human well-being today and in the future; fashion and personal fashion preferences''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Vocabulary for body parts
Nouns: A forehead, an eyebrow, an eyelash, a chin, a chest, lips, a tongue. Vocabulary for human illnesses and diseases:
Nouns: A cold, flu, a fever, a cough, a headache, a stomach ache, a sore throat, a toothache, a backache, an earache, an allergy, an allergic reaction, diabetes, COVID, acne, malaria, chickenpox, measles, a painkiller, an emergency. Verbs: To vomit, to feel dizzy, to breathe.
Adjectives: Painful.
Vocabulary for human nature and human well-being today and in the future:
Nouns: Empathy, social connection, happiness, global citizenship, digital detox, sustainability, self-care. Adjectives: Ambitious, compassionate, courageous.
Vocabulary for fashion and personal fashion preferences
Nouns: (Accessories): A scarf, a headscarf, a necklace, earrings, a bracelet, a ring, a watch, a belt, a hat, a handbag, a hairband (a headband-AmE), a cap, a benie, a tie, a bow tie, gloves, a backpack (rucksack). Adjectives: (Styles): Stylish, trendy, classy, smart casual, vintage, neat, well-dressed, (Clothing materials): denim, leather, cotton. (Clothing patterns): floral, striped, plain, checked, patterned.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, "Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)", "Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)".
*
(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
All future tenses mixed: (revisional): (By next year, she will have improved her health by running every day. She is going to start yoga this weekend to improve flexibility and balance. I will try to stay resilient no matter how difficult things get in the future.)
-
Can for ability (revisional): (I can lift heavy weights with my arms because I work out every day.)
-
Comparative Adjectives (Regular, Irregular) (revisional): (His new haircut looks better than his previous style. She is more ambitious than anyone in her social circle.)
-
The Simple Present vs Present Progressive for Future: (She exercises every morning to keep fit and healthy. She is exercising at the gym right now to stay fit.)
-
Should for Advice: (You should wear a scarf in winter to protect your neck from cold winds.)
-
Could for ability: (She could run a marathon if she trains her legs and increases her endurance.)
-
Adjectives (regular, -ing ending, -ed ending): (She has a beautiful face with sparkling eyes. The patient felt dizzy after experiencing a high fever. Her amazing energy inspires everyone in her fashion design team. After running for an hour, he felt exhausted and his legs were sore).
-
As…as, same…as, like, alike: (My sister’s hair is as long as mine, both silky and healthy. Her style is similar to a vintage fashion icon, effortlessly chic.)
Functions of the Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Use of the Simple Present vs. the Present Progressive for Future: Expressing scheduled or timetabled future events (Simple Present); expressing current intentions, ongoing plans, or arrangements for the near future. (Present Progressive).
Use of All Future Tenses (Mixed) (revisional): Expressing various degrees of certainty, intention, probability, and aspirations about future actions, events, and plans.
-
Use of modal “Should” for Advice: Giving suggestions, advice, and recommendations about what is right or appropriate.
-
Use of modal “Can” for Ability: Expressing past abilities, hypothetical situations, and future possibilities.
-
Use of modal “Could” for Ability: Expressing present or future abilities, skills or possibilities.
-
Use of Adjectives (Regular, -ing ending, -ed ending): Describing characteristics, emotions, and states (regular adjectives); describing ongoing actions or experiences (adjectives with -ing endings); describing feelings or states resulting from experiences (adjectives with -ed endings).
-
Use of Comparative Adjectives (Regular, Irregular): Comparing two things in terms of greater or lesser degree.
-
Use of “As…as, Same…as, Like, Alike”: Expressing similarity, comparison, and likeness between objects, actions, or people; describing similarities in personal habits.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
At last, you’re here in the flesh!
Let’s break the leg for the concert tonight! Oh, my God! I’m in her bad books!
My grandpa is fit as a fiddle despite his age! I’m feeling in the pink and ready to study!
Target Phonetical Sounds in Use
Vowels: e: (/e/; /i:/, /ə/)
Consonants: f: (/f/), g: (/g/, /dʒ/), h: (/h/)
*
(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme.)

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students create a project titled ''Personal Life and Well-Being'' focusing on the body parts, human illnesses and diseases; human nature and well-being today and in the future; and fashion and personal preferences. Students begin by exploring the human body and describing key body parts and their functions. They then discuss common illnesses and diseases, including ways to stay healthy and prevent these conditions according to their ages and levels. Then, students reflect on human well-being, comparing how people maintain physical and mental health today versus what it might look like in the future. Finally, students explore the role of fashion in personal identity by describing their fashion preferences and how clothing choices affect confidence and self-expression. The project can include written descriptions, illustrations, or creative presentations, such as posters or digital slideshows. Students will present their findings in class. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.
EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
Expansion
Objective: To talk about human nature and human well-being today and in the future; fashion and personal fashion preferences in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity 1: Future Well-being Plan
Students individually create a future lifestyle plan that focuses on personal health, fashion preferences, and sustainability, including details about diet, exercise, digital habits, and fashion choices. For example, a student might write, ''In 2030, I will exercise five times a week to stay healthy and choose sustainable, cotton-based clothing to protect the environment''. After preparing their plans, students present them in small groups, comparing their ideas using sentences such as, ''This plan is more suitable (sustainable) than my current lifestyle'', or ''It will be as trendy as fast fashion but more eco-friendly''. In the end, the teacher gives feedback on pronunciation, the use of target vocabulary, and target grammar. The students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
Supporting
Objective: To talk about human illnesses, diseases and give advice in English through a role play activity by using the target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Doctor & Patient Role-Play
Students work in pairs with predetermined roles: Student A as the ''Doctor'' and Student B as the ''Patient''. The teacher prepares papers with symptoms and related advice (e.g., ''headache—take a painkiller'') and places them in a box. Each pair selects a paper. The ''Patient'' uses the symptom to explain their problem (e.g., ''I have a headache''), and the ''Doctor'' gives advice based on the paper (e.g., ''You should take a painkiller''). After each pair performs, the teacher and other students provide constructive and supportive feedback on pronunciation and sentence accuracy. The students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

plan.KONU:
Sub-themes: "Body parts, human illnesses and diseases; human nature and human well-being today and in the future; fashion and personal fashion preferences''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Vocabulary for body parts
Nouns: A forehead, an eyebrow, an eyelash, a chin, a chest, lips, a tongue. Vocabulary for human illnesses and diseases:
Nouns: A cold, flu, a fever, a cough, a headache, a stomach ache, a sore throat, a toothache, a backache, an earache, an allergy, an allergic reaction, diabetes, COVID, acne, malaria, chickenpox, measles, a painkiller, an emergency. Verbs: To vomit, to feel dizzy, to breathe.
Adjectives: Painful.
Vocabulary for human nature and human well-being today and in the future:
Nouns: Empathy, social connection, happiness, global citizenship, digital detox, sustainability, self-care. Adjectives: Ambitious, compassionate, courageous.
Vocabulary for fashion and personal fashion preferences
Nouns: (Accessories): A scarf, a headscarf, a necklace, earrings, a bracelet, a ring, a watch, a belt, a hat, a handbag, a hairband (a headband-AmE), a cap, a benie, a tie, a bow tie, gloves, a backpack (rucksack). Adjectives: (Styles): Stylish, trendy, classy, smart casual, vintage, neat, well-dressed, (Clothing materials): denim, leather, cotton. (Clothing patterns): floral, striped, plain, checked, patterned.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, "Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)", "Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)".
*
(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
All future tenses mixed: (revisional): (By next year, she will have improved her health by running every day. She is going to start yoga this weekend to improve flexibility and balance. I will try to stay resilient no matter how difficult things get in the future.)
-
Can for ability (revisional): (I can lift heavy weights with my arms because I work out every day.)
-
Comparative Adjectives (Regular, Irregular) (revisional): (His new haircut looks better than his previous style. She is more ambitious than anyone in her social circle.)
-
The Simple Present vs Present Progressive for Future: (She exercises every morning to keep fit and healthy. She is exercising at the gym right now to stay fit.)
-
Should for Advice: (You should wear a scarf in winter to protect your neck from cold winds.)
-
Could for ability: (She could run a marathon if she trains her legs and increases her endurance.)
-
Adjectives (regular, -ing ending, -ed ending): (She has a beautiful face with sparkling eyes. The patient felt dizzy after experiencing a high fever. Her amazing energy inspires everyone in her fashion design team. After running for an hour, he felt exhausted and his legs were sore).
-
As…as, same…as, like, alike: (My sister’s hair is as long as mine, both silky and healthy. Her style is similar to a vintage fashion icon, effortlessly chic.)
Functions of the Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Use of the Simple Present vs. the Present Progressive for Future: Expressing scheduled or timetabled future events (Simple Present); expressing current intentions, ongoing plans, or arrangements for the near future. (Present Progressive).
Use of All Future Tenses (Mixed) (revisional): Expressing various degrees of certainty, intention, probability, and aspirations about future actions, events, and plans.
-
Use of modal “Should” for Advice: Giving suggestions, advice, and recommendations about what is right or appropriate.
-
Use of modal “Can” for Ability: Expressing past abilities, hypothetical situations, and future possibilities.
-
Use of modal “Could” for Ability: Expressing present or future abilities, skills or possibilities.
-
Use of Adjectives (Regular, -ing ending, -ed ending): Describing characteristics, emotions, and states (regular adjectives); describing ongoing actions or experiences (adjectives with -ing endings); describing feelings or states resulting from experiences (adjectives with -ed endings).
-
Use of Comparative Adjectives (Regular, Irregular): Comparing two things in terms of greater or lesser degree.
-
Use of “As…as, Same…as, Like, Alike”: Expressing similarity, comparison, and likeness between objects, actions, or people; describing similarities in personal habits.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
At last, you’re here in the flesh!
Let’s break the leg for the concert tonight! Oh, my God! I’m in her bad books!
My grandpa is fit as a fiddle despite his age! I’m feeling in the pink and ready to study!
Target Phonetical Sounds in Use
Vowels: e: (/e/; /i:/, /ə/)
Consonants: f: (/f/), g: (/g/, /dʒ/), h: (/h/)
*
(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme.)

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students create a project titled ''Personal Life and Well-Being'' focusing on the body parts, human illnesses and diseases; human nature and well-being today and in the future; and fashion and personal preferences. Students begin by exploring the human body and describing key body parts and their functions. They then discuss common illnesses and diseases, including ways to stay healthy and prevent these conditions according to their ages and levels. Then, students reflect on human well-being, comparing how people maintain physical and mental health today versus what it might look like in the future. Finally, students explore the role of fashion in personal identity by describing their fashion preferences and how clothing choices affect confidence and self-expression. The project can include written descriptions, illustrations, or creative presentations, such as posters or digital slideshows. Students will present their findings in class. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.
EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
Expansion
Objective: To talk about human nature and human well-being today and in the future; fashion and personal fashion preferences in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity 1: Future Well-being Plan
Students individually create a future lifestyle plan that focuses on personal health, fashion preferences, and sustainability, including details about diet, exercise, digital habits, and fashion choices. For example, a student might write, ''In 2030, I will exercise five times a week to stay healthy and choose sustainable, cotton-based clothing to protect the environment''. After preparing their plans, students present them in small groups, comparing their ideas using sentences such as, ''This plan is more suitable (sustainable) than my current lifestyle'', or ''It will be as trendy as fast fashion but more eco-friendly''. In the end, the teacher gives feedback on pronunciation, the use of target vocabulary, and target grammar. The students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
Supporting
Objective: To talk about human illnesses, diseases and give advice in English through a role play activity by using the target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Doctor & Patient Role-Play
Students work in pairs with predetermined roles: Student A as the ''Doctor'' and Student B as the ''Patient''. The teacher prepares papers with symptoms and related advice (e.g., ''headache—take a painkiller'') and places them in a box. Each pair selects a paper. The ''Patient'' uses the symptom to explain their problem (e.g., ''I have a headache''), and the ''Doctor'' gives advice based on the paper (e.g., ''You should take a painkiller''). After each pair performs, the teacher and other students provide constructive and supportive feedback on pronunciation and sentence accuracy. The students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

"
Sub-themes: ''Family members and their daily routines today and in the past; hobbies and interests of family members (sports & films); different types of houses and families from the world''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Vocabulary for family members and their daily routines
Nouns: (revisional) a great-grandmother/father, a mother / father /brother /sister / daughter /son-in-law, a half-sister/brother, (target) a sibling, a distant relative. Verbs: To run errands, to commute, to do household chores, to do the dusting, to do the laundry, to set the table, to empty the dishwasher, to do the ironing.
Types of families
Nouns: A single-parent family, an immediate family, a family, a nuclear family. Vocabulary for different types of houses and families from the world:
Types of houses
Nouns: (revisional) a detached house, a semi-detached house, a cottage, villa, a terraced house, (target) an attached house, an igloo, a hut, a houseboat, a farmhouse, a treehouse.
Vocabulary for hobbies and interests of family members (sports & films):
Sports
Nouns: Playing badminton, to go cycling / running / jogging / hiking / trekking / rafting / swimming / surfing / skating / skiing / snowboarding, to ride a horse, to do archery, to do extreme sports.
Vocabulary for film genres
Nouns: Science fiction (sci-fi), thrillers, horror films, documentaries, (target) romantic comedies, sitcoms.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, ""Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)"", ""Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)"".
*
(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
The Simple Past Tense (to be: Was/Were, There was/There were) (Regular, Irregular verbs): (Yesterday, there was a big family gathering at our detached house. My sisters were very hardworking; they prepared meals, tidied up, and set the table every day. My brother played basketball every weekend when he was younger.)
-
Question tags: (Your sibling likes watching science fiction films as a teenager, doesn’t she?)
-
Could for ability: (My sister could ride a horse very well when she was younger. My father could do archery when he was a teenager living in the countryside.)
-
Used to: (When I was a child, we used to live in a small cottage in the mountains. My great-grandmother used to wake up at 5 a.m. every day to do the cleaning and washing up.)
Functions of the Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Use of the Simple Past Tense (to be: was/were, there was/were) Regular,irregularverbs:Describingactions,statesand/oreventsthathappenedandwerecompletedinthepast.
-
Use of “Question Tags” with the Simple Past Tense: Seeking information about people, actions, or events, whether they happened in the past.
-
Use of Modal “Could” for ability (in the past): Expressing past or present abilities, skills, and/or possibilities.
-
Use of “Used to”: Describing habits, or states that were true in the past but are no longer the case.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
Cheers for helping me!
Keep your chin up!
She’s under the weather because of her problems!
The exam was just a doodle!
You always pull my leg!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use
Vowel: i (/aı/, /ı/, /i:/)
Consonants: j (/dʒeɪ/, /dʒ/); k: (/k/); l: (/ɛl/ /l/)
*
(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme.)"

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students will create a project titled "Family Life and Home," exploring the dynamics of family life across time and cultures. They will begin by describing the daily routines of their family members, comparing these routines to those of previous generations to highlight how roles and responsibilities have evolved. Next, they will focus on hobbies and interests within the family, such as favourite sports or films, and explain how these activities contribute to relations and personal expression. Finally, students will research different types of houses and family structures around the world, comparing them to their own experiences and reflecting on how cultural differences influence family life and home environments. The project should include creative elements such as family interviews, photos, drawings, or videos and will be presented in class. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.
EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
Expansion
Objective: To talk about past and present routines in English through reading skills by using the target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Family Routines - Information Gap Reading
Students work in groups of 3-4. Each student receives a different part of a reading text about a family’s daily routines today and in the past (e.g., great-grandmother’s routine, sibling’s routine, etc.). The group is also given a blank table with headings like Family Member, Past Routine, and Present Routine. One student, who does not read the text, acts as the recorder and asks questions to the others (e.g., ''What did the great- grandmother use to do in the morning?''). The others share information from their sections to fill in the table collaboratively. As groups work, the teacher moves around, listening to pronunciation and checking the accuracy of responses, and s/he provides supportive feedback. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
Supporting
Objective: To compare past and present routines in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity: Past and Present Routines
The teacher writes daily routines (e.g., wake up, vacuum the house) on papers and places them in a box. As an example, the teacher picks a paper (e.g., wake up), forms sentences comparing past and present routines using ''used to'' (e.g., ''I used to wake up at 6 am. Now, I wake up at 7 am'') and s/he writes them on the board. Then, students take turns picking a paper, forming similar sentences, and sharing them with the class. The teacher provides constructive and supportive feedback on accuracy and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

Sub-themes: ''Family members and their daily routines today and in the past; hobbies and interests of family members (sports & films); different types of houses and families from the world''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Vocabulary for family members and their daily routines
Nouns: (revisional) a great-grandmother/father, a mother / father /brother /sister / daughter /son-in-law, a half-sister/brother, (target) a sibling, a distant relative. Verbs: To run errands, to commute, to do household chores, to do the dusting, to do the laundry, to set the table, to empty the dishwasher, to do the ironing.
Types of families
Nouns: A single-parent family, an immediate family, a family, a nuclear family. Vocabulary for different types of houses and families from the world:
Types of houses
Nouns: (revisional) a detached house, a semi-detached house, a cottage, villa, a terraced house, (target) an attached house, an igloo, a hut, a houseboat, a farmhouse, a treehouse.
Vocabulary for hobbies and interests of family members (sports & films):
Sports
Nouns: Playing badminton, to go cycling / running / jogging / hiking / trekking / rafting / swimming / surfing / skating / skiing / snowboarding, to ride a horse, to do archery, to do extreme sports.
Vocabulary for film genres
Nouns: Science fiction (sci-fi), thrillers, horror films, documentaries, (target) romantic comedies, sitcoms.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, "Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)", "Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)".
*
(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
The Simple Past Tense (to be: Was/Were, There was/There were) (Regular, Irregular verbs): (Yesterday, there was a big family gathering at our detached house. My sisters were very hardworking; they prepared meals, tidied up, and set the table every day. My brother played basketball every weekend when he was younger.)
-
Question tags: (Your sibling likes watching science fiction films as a teenager, doesn’t she?)
-
Could for ability: (My sister could ride a horse very well when she was younger. My father could do archery when he was a teenager living in the countryside.)
-
Used to: (When I was a child, we used to live in a small cottage in the mountains. My great-grandmother used to wake up at 5 a.m. every day to do the cleaning and washing up.)
Functions of the Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Use of the Simple Past Tense (to be: was/were, there was/were) Regular,irregularverbs:Describingactions,statesand/oreventsthathappenedandwerecompletedinthepast.
-
Use of “Question Tags” with the Simple Past Tense: Seeking information about people, actions, or events, whether they happened in the past.
-
Use of Modal “Could” for ability (in the past): Expressing past or present abilities, skills, and/or possibilities.
-
Use of “Used to”: Describing habits, or states that were true in the past but are no longer the case.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
Cheers for helping me!
Keep your chin up!
She’s under the weather because of her problems!
The exam was just a doodle!
You always pull my leg!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use
Vowel: i (/aı/, /ı/, /i:/)
Consonants: j (/dʒeɪ/, /dʒ/); k: (/k/); l: (/ɛl/ /l/)
*
(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme.)

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students will create a project titled "Family Life and Home," exploring the dynamics of family life across time and cultures. They will begin by describing the daily routines of their family members, comparing these routines to those of previous generations to highlight how roles and responsibilities have evolved. Next, they will focus on hobbies and interests within the family, such as favourite sports or films, and explain how these activities contribute to relations and personal expression. Finally, students will research different types of houses and family structures around the world, comparing them to their own experiences and reflecting on how cultural differences influence family life and home environments. The project should include creative elements such as family interviews, photos, drawings, or videos and will be presented in class. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.
EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
Expansion
Objective: To talk about past and present routines in English through reading skills by using the target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Family Routines - Information Gap Reading
Students work in groups of 3-4. Each student receives a different part of a reading text about a family’s daily routines today and in the past (e.g., great-grandmother’s routine, sibling’s routine, etc.). The group is also given a blank table with headings like Family Member, Past Routine, and Present Routine. One student, who does not read the text, acts as the recorder and asks questions to the others (e.g., ''What did the great- grandmother use to do in the morning?''). The others share information from their sections to fill in the table collaboratively. As groups work, the teacher moves around, listening to pronunciation and checking the accuracy of responses, and s/he provides supportive feedback. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
Supporting
Objective: To compare past and present routines in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity: Past and Present Routines
The teacher writes daily routines (e.g., wake up, vacuum the house) on papers and places them in a box. As an example, the teacher picks a paper (e.g., wake up), forms sentences comparing past and present routines using ''used to'' (e.g., ''I used to wake up at 6 am. Now, I wake up at 7 am'') and s/he writes them on the board. Then, students take turns picking a paper, forming similar sentences, and sharing them with the class. The teacher provides constructive and supportive feedback on accuracy and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

plan.KONU:
Sub-themes: ''Family members and their daily routines today and in the past; hobbies and interests of family members (sports & films); different types of houses and families from the world''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Vocabulary for family members and their daily routines
Nouns: (revisional) a great-grandmother/father, a mother / father /brother /sister / daughter /son-in-law, a half-sister/brother, (target) a sibling, a distant relative. Verbs: To run errands, to commute, to do household chores, to do the dusting, to do the laundry, to set the table, to empty the dishwasher, to do the ironing.
Types of families
Nouns: A single-parent family, an immediate family, a family, a nuclear family. Vocabulary for different types of houses and families from the world:
Types of houses
Nouns: (revisional) a detached house, a semi-detached house, a cottage, villa, a terraced house, (target) an attached house, an igloo, a hut, a houseboat, a farmhouse, a treehouse.
Vocabulary for hobbies and interests of family members (sports & films):
Sports
Nouns: Playing badminton, to go cycling / running / jogging / hiking / trekking / rafting / swimming / surfing / skating / skiing / snowboarding, to ride a horse, to do archery, to do extreme sports.
Vocabulary for film genres
Nouns: Science fiction (sci-fi), thrillers, horror films, documentaries, (target) romantic comedies, sitcoms.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, "Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)", "Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)".
*
(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
The Simple Past Tense (to be: Was/Were, There was/There were) (Regular, Irregular verbs): (Yesterday, there was a big family gathering at our detached house. My sisters were very hardworking; they prepared meals, tidied up, and set the table every day. My brother played basketball every weekend when he was younger.)
-
Question tags: (Your sibling likes watching science fiction films as a teenager, doesn’t she?)
-
Could for ability: (My sister could ride a horse very well when she was younger. My father could do archery when he was a teenager living in the countryside.)
-
Used to: (When I was a child, we used to live in a small cottage in the mountains. My great-grandmother used to wake up at 5 a.m. every day to do the cleaning and washing up.)
Functions of the Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Use of the Simple Past Tense (to be: was/were, there was/were) Regular,irregularverbs:Describingactions,statesand/oreventsthathappenedandwerecompletedinthepast.
-
Use of “Question Tags” with the Simple Past Tense: Seeking information about people, actions, or events, whether they happened in the past.
-
Use of Modal “Could” for ability (in the past): Expressing past or present abilities, skills, and/or possibilities.
-
Use of “Used to”: Describing habits, or states that were true in the past but are no longer the case.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
Cheers for helping me!
Keep your chin up!
She’s under the weather because of her problems!
The exam was just a doodle!
You always pull my leg!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use
Vowel: i (/aı/, /ı/, /i:/)
Consonants: j (/dʒeɪ/, /dʒ/); k: (/k/); l: (/ɛl/ /l/)
*
(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme.)

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students will create a project titled "Family Life and Home," exploring the dynamics of family life across time and cultures. They will begin by describing the daily routines of their family members, comparing these routines to those of previous generations to highlight how roles and responsibilities have evolved. Next, they will focus on hobbies and interests within the family, such as favourite sports or films, and explain how these activities contribute to relations and personal expression. Finally, students will research different types of houses and family structures around the world, comparing them to their own experiences and reflecting on how cultural differences influence family life and home environments. The project should include creative elements such as family interviews, photos, drawings, or videos and will be presented in class. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.
EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
Expansion
Objective: To talk about past and present routines in English through reading skills by using the target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Family Routines - Information Gap Reading
Students work in groups of 3-4. Each student receives a different part of a reading text about a family’s daily routines today and in the past (e.g., great-grandmother’s routine, sibling’s routine, etc.). The group is also given a blank table with headings like Family Member, Past Routine, and Present Routine. One student, who does not read the text, acts as the recorder and asks questions to the others (e.g., ''What did the great- grandmother use to do in the morning?''). The others share information from their sections to fill in the table collaboratively. As groups work, the teacher moves around, listening to pronunciation and checking the accuracy of responses, and s/he provides supportive feedback. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
Supporting
Objective: To compare past and present routines in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity: Past and Present Routines
The teacher writes daily routines (e.g., wake up, vacuum the house) on papers and places them in a box. As an example, the teacher picks a paper (e.g., wake up), forms sentences comparing past and present routines using ''used to'' (e.g., ''I used to wake up at 6 am. Now, I wake up at 7 am'') and s/he writes them on the board. Then, students take turns picking a paper, forming similar sentences, and sharing them with the class. The teacher provides constructive and supportive feedback on accuracy and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

plan.KONU:
Sub-themes: ''Family members and their daily routines today and in the past; hobbies and interests of family members (sports & films); different types of houses and families from the world''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Vocabulary for family members and their daily routines
Nouns: (revisional) a great-grandmother/father, a mother / father /brother /sister / daughter /son-in-law, a half-sister/brother, (target) a sibling, a distant relative. Verbs: To run errands, to commute, to do household chores, to do the dusting, to do the laundry, to set the table, to empty the dishwasher, to do the ironing.
Types of families
Nouns: A single-parent family, an immediate family, a family, a nuclear family. Vocabulary for different types of houses and families from the world:
Types of houses
Nouns: (revisional) a detached house, a semi-detached house, a cottage, villa, a terraced house, (target) an attached house, an igloo, a hut, a houseboat, a farmhouse, a treehouse.
Vocabulary for hobbies and interests of family members (sports & films):
Sports
Nouns: Playing badminton, to go cycling / running / jogging / hiking / trekking / rafting / swimming / surfing / skating / skiing / snowboarding, to ride a horse, to do archery, to do extreme sports.
Vocabulary for film genres
Nouns: Science fiction (sci-fi), thrillers, horror films, documentaries, (target) romantic comedies, sitcoms.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, "Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)", "Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)".
*
(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
The Simple Past Tense (to be: Was/Were, There was/There were) (Regular, Irregular verbs): (Yesterday, there was a big family gathering at our detached house. My sisters were very hardworking; they prepared meals, tidied up, and set the table every day. My brother played basketball every weekend when he was younger.)
-
Question tags: (Your sibling likes watching science fiction films as a teenager, doesn’t she?)
-
Could for ability: (My sister could ride a horse very well when she was younger. My father could do archery when he was a teenager living in the countryside.)
-
Used to: (When I was a child, we used to live in a small cottage in the mountains. My great-grandmother used to wake up at 5 a.m. every day to do the cleaning and washing up.)
Functions of the Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Use of the Simple Past Tense (to be: was/were, there was/were) Regular,irregularverbs:Describingactions,statesand/oreventsthathappenedandwerecompletedinthepast.
-
Use of “Question Tags” with the Simple Past Tense: Seeking information about people, actions, or events, whether they happened in the past.
-
Use of Modal “Could” for ability (in the past): Expressing past or present abilities, skills, and/or possibilities.
-
Use of “Used to”: Describing habits, or states that were true in the past but are no longer the case.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
Cheers for helping me!
Keep your chin up!
She’s under the weather because of her problems!
The exam was just a doodle!
You always pull my leg!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use
Vowel: i (/aı/, /ı/, /i:/)
Consonants: j (/dʒeɪ/, /dʒ/); k: (/k/); l: (/ɛl/ /l/)
*
(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme.)

Transportation: A bus, a train, a bike / bicycle, a taxi, on foot, a car, an aeroplane (air-plane-AmE).

Verbs: To surf the Net, to chill out, to buy popcorn/ snacks, to attend fitness classes, to join tournaments, to do Pilates.

Nouns: A first-aid kit, a bandage. Verbs: To buy medicine, to ask for advice, to buy health products/ vitamins, to check blood pressure, to attend check-ups, to browse (in a chemist’s)
Vocabulary for pros and cons of different types of transportation in the neighbourhood and city:
Transportation: Nouns: Public transport, an underground (subway- AmE), a ferry, a motorbike, a tram, a ship, a lorry (truck-AmE), e-scooters.
Pros and cons: Adjectives: Eco-friendly, reliable, efficient, affordable, convenient, time-saving, timeconsuming, polluting, unsafe, uncomfortable, (prone to) delays.
-
The Past Progressive Tense: (I was going to the school by bike yesterday morning. I was going to school on foot while you were taking the bus last morning.)
-
The Simple Past Tense vs Past Progressive Tense: (The doctor was checking my blood pressure when you called me.)
-
Question tags: (You came to school on foot yesterday, didn’t you? There wasn’t a traffic jam two hours ago, was there?)
Use of the Past Progressive Tense: Describing an action or other actions that are in progress in the past. Use of The Simple Past Tense vs Past Progressive Tense: Contrasting a completed action at specified time in the past with an action in progress at an exact moment in the past.
Use of Question Tags for The Simple Past Tense & The Past Progressive Tense: Confirming or clarifying past events.
I need to pop to the market!
This city is full of cool sights!
Let’s catch the bus!
What a traffic jam!
The Topkapı Palace is a must-see in İstanbul!”

EK_ALANLAR.Okul Temelli Planlama:
Okul temelli planlama; zümre öğretmenler kurulu tarafından ders kapsamında gerçekleştirilmesi kararlaştırılan araştırma ve gözlem, sosyal etkinlikler, proje çalışmaları, yerel çalışmalar, okuma çalışmaları vb. çalışmaları kapsamaktadır. Çalışmalar için ayrılan süre eğitim-öğretim yılı içinde planlanır ve yıllık planlarda ifade edilir.
Bu planlamalar kapsamında yürütülecek öğretim faaliyetleri; öğrenci katılımını desteklemeli, yaparak ve yaşayarak öğrenmeye olanak tanımalı, öğrencinin bütüncül gelişime hizmet etmelidir. *Bu çerçeve planda belirtilen okul temelli planlama haftaları örnek olarak sunulmuştur. Zümre öğretmenler kurulunda aldığınız karara göre okul ve ders koşullarınıza uygun (öğretim programında belirtilen okul temelli planlama ders saati 2 haftadan fazla sürebilir) düzenleyebilirsiniz.

a)

d)

a)

c)
Students make significant and necessary comparisons in the generally perceived current content to highlight differences between two or more different things by using visuals, ensuring clarity and meaning.
d)
Students recognise significant branching, linear or spiral relationships (if any) within the generally perceived current content.
e)

g)

h)

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students will create a project titled "Family Life and Home," exploring the dynamics of family life across time and cultures. They will begin by describing the daily routines of their family members, comparing these routines to those of previous generations to highlight how roles and responsibilities have evolved. Next, they will focus on hobbies and interests within the family, such as favourite sports or films, and explain how these activities contribute to relations and personal expression. Finally, students will research different types of houses and family structures around the world, comparing them to their own experiences and reflecting on how cultural differences influence family life and home environments. The project should include creative elements such as family interviews, photos, drawings, or videos and will be presented in class. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students conduct an interview with a person from their neighbourhood such as a driver, a chemist, a neighbour, an officer etc. about past experiences of these people in the city in terms of public transportation, the pros and cons of different types of transportation in the neighbourhood and city, getting help from services in the neighbourhood and the city and social life. Students begin by preparing interview questions. Next, they elicit and decide the questions. Then, they choose the person for the interview. They may use avatars or AI to create characters for the interviews. The interview should include creative elements, such as charts, or videos, and students will present their findings in class. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.
EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
Expansion
Objective: To talk about past and present routines in English through reading skills by using the target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Family Routines - Information Gap Reading
Students work in groups of 3-4. Each student receives a different part of a reading text about a family’s daily routines today and in the past (e.g., great-grandmother’s routine, sibling’s routine, etc.). The group is also given a blank table with headings like Family Member, Past Routine, and Present Routine. One student, who does not read the text, acts as the recorder and asks questions to the others (e.g., ''What did the great- grandmother use to do in the morning?''). The others share information from their sections to fill in the table collaboratively. As groups work, the teacher moves around, listening to pronunciation and checking the accuracy of responses, and s/he provides supportive feedback. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
Supporting
Objective: To compare past and present routines in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity: Past and Present Routines
The teacher writes daily routines (e.g., wake up, vacuum the house) on papers and places them in a box. As an example, the teacher picks a paper (e.g., wake up), forms sentences comparing past and present routines using ''used to'' (e.g., ''I used to wake up at 6 am. Now, I wake up at 7 am'') and s/he writes them on the board. Then, students take turns picking a paper, forming similar sentences, and sharing them with the class. The teacher provides constructive and supportive feedback on accuracy and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
Objective:
To talk about activities, services, and transportation options in the city and neighbourhood by listing pros and cons in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity 1: City Life
Discussions The teacher divides the class into three groups with specific topics: Group 1: Activities in attractions and recreational places (e.g., cafés, cinemas, gyms). Group 2: Getting help from services in the neighbourhood and city (e.g., pharmacies, hospitals). Group 3: Pros and cons of different types of transportation in the neighbourhood and city. Each group creates a list of pros and cons using the target vocabulary (e.g., ''Public transport saves time but is often crowded'', or ''Chatting with friends at a café feels relaxing but can be expensive''). Groups present their ideas to the class, and other students ask questions such as, ''Why do you think it is reliable?'' or ''Isn’t it time-consuming?'' After the discussion, each student writes a short paragraph and explains if s/he agrees or disagrees with one idea and why. The teacher provides feedback on accuracy, use of target vocabulary, and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
To describe past activities in different places in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity 1: What Were We Doing?
The teacher writes some target words on the board for different places: At the café: drinking tea, chatting with friends. At the gym: lifting weights, doing pilates. At the cinema: watching a movie, eating popcorn. The teacher gives an example and writes it on the board: ''I was drinking tea at the cafe''. Then, students come to the board one by one and write their own sentences (e.g., ''We were watching a movie at the cinema''.). Next, the teacher writes a question and answer on the board: ''What were you doing at the cafe?'' ''I was chatting with friends''. Students practise asking and answering questions in a chain drill game format: one student asks the next, and so on. The teacher gives constructive and supportive feedback on accuracy and pronunciation. Students 340 THE ENGLISH LANGUAGE CURRICULUM reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

plan.KONU:
Sub-themes: ''Activities to do in attractions (cafes, cinemas; gyms, sports clubs); getting help from services (pharmacies, hospitals, etc.); pros and cons of different types of transportation in the neighbourhood and city''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Transportation: A bus, a train, a bike / bicycle, a taxi, on foot, a car, an aeroplane (air-plane-AmE).
Vocabulary for activities to do in attractions and recreational places in the neighbourhood and city (cafes, cinemas; gyms, sports clubs):
Verbs: To surf the Net, to chill out, to buy popcorn/ snacks, to attend fitness classes, to join tournaments, to do Pilates.
Vocabulary for getting help from services in the neighbourhood and the city (pharmacies, hospitals etc):
Nouns: A first-aid kit, a bandage. Verbs: To buy medicine, to ask for advice, to buy health products/ vitamins, to check blood pressure, to attend check-ups, to browse (in a chemist’s)
Vocabulary for pros and cons of different types of transportation in the neighbourhood and city:
Transportation: Nouns: Public transport, an underground (subway- AmE), a ferry, a motorbike, a tram, a ship, a lorry (truck-AmE), e-scooters.
Pros and cons: Adjectives: Eco-friendly, reliable, efficient, affordable, convenient, time-saving, timeconsuming, polluting, unsafe, uncomfortable, (prone to) delays.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
The Past Progressive Tense: (I was going to the school by bike yesterday morning. I was going to school on foot while you were taking the bus last morning.)
-
The Simple Past Tense vs Past Progressive Tense: (The doctor was checking my blood pressure when you called me.)
-
Question tags: (You came to school on foot yesterday, didn’t you? There wasn’t a traffic jam two hours ago, was there?)
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, "Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)", "Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)".
*
(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Functions of the Target Grammatical Structures in Use
Use of the Past Progressive Tense: Describing an action or other actions that are in progress in the past. Use of The Simple Past Tense vs Past Progressive Tense: Contrasting a completed action at specified time in the past with an action in progress at an exact moment in the past.
Use of Question Tags for The Simple Past Tense & The Past Progressive Tense: Confirming or clarifying past events.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
I need to pop to the market!
This city is full of cool sights!
Let’s catch the bus!
What a traffic jam!
The Topkapı Palace is a must-see in İstanbul!”
Target Phonological Sounds in Use
Vowel: o: (/əʊ/, /ɒ/, /əʊ/)
Consonants: m (/ɛm/,/m/); n: (/ɛn/, /n/); p: ( /piː//p/)
*
(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme.)

EK_ALANLAR.Okul Temelli Planlama:
Okul temelli planlama; zümre öğretmenler kurulu tarafından ders kapsamında gerçekleştirilmesi kararlaştırılan araştırma ve gözlem, sosyal etkinlikler, proje çalışmaları, yerel çalışmalar, okuma çalışmaları vb. çalışmaları kapsamaktadır. Çalışmalar için ayrılan süre eğitim-öğretim yılı içinde planlanır ve yıllık planlarda ifade edilir.
Bu planlamalar kapsamında yürütülecek öğretim faaliyetleri; öğrenci katılımını desteklemeli, yaparak ve yaşayarak öğrenmeye olanak tanımalı, öğrencinin bütüncül gelişime hizmet etmelidir. *Bu çerçeve planda belirtilen okul temelli planlama haftaları örnek olarak sunulmuştur. Zümre öğretmenler kurulunda aldığınız karara göre okul ve ders koşullarınıza uygun (öğretim programında belirtilen okul temelli planlama ders saati 2 haftadan fazla sürebilir) düzenleyebilirsiniz.

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students conduct an interview with a person from their neighbourhood such as a driver, a chemist, a neighbour, an officer etc. about past experiences of these people in the city in terms of public transportation, the pros and cons of different types of transportation in the neighbourhood and city, getting help from services in the neighbourhood and the city and social life. Students begin by preparing interview questions. Next, they elicit and decide the questions. Then, they choose the person for the interview. They may use avatars or AI to create characters for the interviews. The interview should include creative elements, such as charts, or videos, and students will present their findings in class. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.
EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
Expansion
Objective:
To talk about activities, services, and transportation options in the city and neighbourhood by listing pros and cons in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity 1: City Life
Discussions The teacher divides the class into three groups with specific topics: Group 1: Activities in attractions and recreational places (e.g., cafés, cinemas, gyms). Group 2: Getting help from services in the neighbourhood and city (e.g., pharmacies, hospitals). Group 3: Pros and cons of different types of transportation in the neighbourhood and city. Each group creates a list of pros and cons using the target vocabulary (e.g., ''Public transport saves time but is often crowded'', or ''Chatting with friends at a café feels relaxing but can be expensive''). Groups present their ideas to the class, and other students ask questions such as, ''Why do you think it is reliable?'' or ''Isn’t it time-consuming?'' After the discussion, each student writes a short paragraph and explains if s/he agrees or disagrees with one idea and why. The teacher provides feedback on accuracy, use of target vocabulary, and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
Supporting
Objective:
To describe past activities in different places in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity 1: What Were We Doing?
The teacher writes some target words on the board for different places: At the café: drinking tea, chatting with friends. At the gym: lifting weights, doing pilates. At the cinema: watching a movie, eating popcorn. The teacher gives an example and writes it on the board: ''I was drinking tea at the cafe''. Then, students come to the board one by one and write their own sentences (e.g., ''We were watching a movie at the cinema''.). Next, the teacher writes a question and answer on the board: ''What were you doing at the cafe?'' ''I was chatting with friends''. Students practise asking and answering questions in a chain drill game format: one student asks the next, and so on. The teacher gives constructive and supportive feedback on accuracy and pronunciation. Students 340 THE ENGLISH LANGUAGE CURRICULUM reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

plan.KONU:
"Sub-themes: ''Activities to do in attractions (cafes, cinemas; gyms, sports clubs); getting help from services (pharmacies, hospitals, etc.); pros and cons of different types of transportation in the neighbourhood and city''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Transportation: A bus, a train, a bike / bicycle, a taxi, on foot, a car, an aeroplane (air-plane-AmE).
Vocabulary for activities to do in attractions and recreational places in the neighbourhood and city (cafes, cinemas; gyms, sports clubs):
Verbs: To surf the Net, to chill out, to buy popcorn/ snacks, to attend fitness classes, to join tournaments, to do Pilates.
Vocabulary for getting help from services in the neighbourhood and the city (pharmacies, hospitals etc):
Nouns: A first-aid kit, a bandage. Verbs: To buy medicine, to ask for advice, to buy health products/ vitamins, to check blood pressure, to attend check-ups, to browse (in a chemist’s)
Vocabulary for pros and cons of different types of transportation in the neighbourhood and city:
Transportation: Nouns: Public transport, an underground (subway- AmE), a ferry, a motorbike, a tram, a ship, a lorry (truck-AmE), e-scooters.
Pros and cons: Adjectives: Eco-friendly, reliable, efficient, affordable, convenient, time-saving, timeconsuming, polluting, unsafe, uncomfortable, (prone to) delays.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
The Past Progressive Tense: (I was going to the school by bike yesterday morning. I was going to school on foot while you were taking the bus last morning.)
-
The Simple Past Tense vs Past Progressive Tense: (The doctor was checking my blood pressure when you called me.)
-
Question tags: (You came to school on foot yesterday, didn’t you? There wasn’t a traffic jam two hours ago, was there?)
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, ""Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)"", ""Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)"".
*
(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Functions of the Target Grammatical Structures in Use
Use of the Past Progressive Tense: Describing an action or other actions that are in progress in the past. Use of The Simple Past Tense vs Past Progressive Tense: Contrasting a completed action at specified time in the past with an action in progress at an exact moment in the past.
Use of Question Tags for The Simple Past Tense & The Past Progressive Tense: Confirming or clarifying past events.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
I need to pop to the market!
This city is full of cool sights!
Let’s catch the bus!
What a traffic jam!
The Topkapı Palace is a must-see in İstanbul!”
Target Phonological Sounds in Use
Vowel: o: (/əʊ/, /ɒ/, /əʊ/)
Consonants: m (/ɛm/,/m/); n: (/ɛn/, /n/); p: ( /piː//p/)
*
(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme.)"

Okul temelli planlama; zümre öğretmenler kurulu tarafından ders kapsamında gerçekleştirilmesi kararlaştırılan araştırma ve gözlem, sosyal etkinlikler, proje çalışmaları, yerel çalışmalar, okuma çalışmaları vb. çalışmaları kapsamaktadır. Çalışmalar için ayrılan süre eğitim-öğretim yılı içinde planlanır ve yıllık planlarda ifade edilir.
Bu planlamalar kapsamında yürütülecek öğretim faaliyetleri; öğrenci katılımını desteklemeli, yaparak ve yaşayarak öğrenmeye olanak tanımalı, öğrencinin bütüncül gelişime hizmet etmelidir. *Bu çerçeve planda belirtilen okul temelli planlama haftaları örnek olarak sunulmuştur. Zümre öğretmenler kurulunda aldığınız karara göre okul ve ders koşullarınıza uygun (öğretim programında belirtilen okul temelli planlama ders saati 2 haftadan fazla sürebilir) düzenleyebilirsiniz.

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
"PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students conduct an interview with a person from their neighbourhood such as a driver, a chemist, a neighbour, an officer etc. about past experiences of these people in the city in terms of public transportation, the pros and cons of different types of transportation in the neighbourhood and city, getting help from services in the neighbourhood and the city and social life. Students begin by preparing interview questions. Next, they elicit and decide the questions. Then, they choose the person for the interview. They may use avatars or AI to create characters for the interviews. The interview should include creative elements, such as charts, or videos, and students will present their findings in class. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme. "
EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
Expansion
Objective:
To talk about activities, services, and transportation options in the city and neighbourhood by listing pros and cons in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity 1: City Life
Discussions The teacher divides the class into three groups with specific topics: Group 1: Activities in attractions and recreational places (e.g., cafés, cinemas, gyms). Group 2: Getting help from services in the neighbourhood and city (e.g., pharmacies, hospitals). Group 3: Pros and cons of different types of transportation in the neighbourhood and city. Each group creates a list of pros and cons using the target vocabulary (e.g., ''Public transport saves time but is often crowded'', or ''Chatting with friends at a café feels relaxing but can be expensive''). Groups present their ideas to the class, and other students ask questions such as, ''Why do you think it is reliable?'' or ''Isn’t it time-consuming?'' After the discussion, each student writes a short paragraph and explains if s/he agrees or disagrees with one idea and why. The teacher provides feedback on accuracy, use of target vocabulary, and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
Supporting
Objective:
To describe past activities in different places in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity 1: What Were We Doing?
The teacher writes some target words on the board for different places: At the café: drinking tea, chatting with friends. At the gym: lifting weights, doing pilates. At the cinema: watching a movie, eating popcorn. The teacher gives an example and writes it on the board: ''I was drinking tea at the cafe''. Then, students come to the board one by one and write their own sentences (e.g., ''We were watching a movie at the cinema''.). Next, the teacher writes a question and answer on the board: ''What were you doing at the cafe?'' ''I was chatting with friends''. Students practise asking and answering questions in a chain drill game format: one student asks the next, and so on. The teacher gives constructive and supportive feedback on accuracy and pronunciation. Students 340 THE ENGLISH LANGUAGE CURRICULUM reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

plan.KONU:
"Sub-themes: ''Activities to do in attractions (cafes, cinemas; gyms, sports clubs); getting help from services (pharmacies, hospitals, etc.); pros and cons of different types of transportation in the neighbourhood and city''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Transportation: A bus, a train, a bike / bicycle, a taxi, on foot, a car, an aeroplane (air-plane-AmE).
Vocabulary for activities to do in attractions and recreational places in the neighbourhood and city (cafes, cinemas; gyms, sports clubs):
Verbs: To surf the Net, to chill out, to buy popcorn/ snacks, to attend fitness classes, to join tournaments, to do Pilates.
Vocabulary for getting help from services in the neighbourhood and the city (pharmacies, hospitals etc):
Nouns: A first-aid kit, a bandage. Verbs: To buy medicine, to ask for advice, to buy health products/ vitamins, to check blood pressure, to attend check-ups, to browse (in a chemist’s)
Vocabulary for pros and cons of different types of transportation in the neighbourhood and city:
Transportation: Nouns: Public transport, an underground (subway- AmE), a ferry, a motorbike, a tram, a ship, a lorry (truck-AmE), e-scooters.
Pros and cons: Adjectives: Eco-friendly, reliable, efficient, affordable, convenient, time-saving, timeconsuming, polluting, unsafe, uncomfortable, (prone to) delays.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
The Past Progressive Tense: (I was going to the school by bike yesterday morning. I was going to school on foot while you were taking the bus last morning.)
-
The Simple Past Tense vs Past Progressive Tense: (The doctor was checking my blood pressure when you called me.)
-
Question tags: (You came to school on foot yesterday, didn’t you? There wasn’t a traffic jam two hours ago, was there?)
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, ""Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)"", ""Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)"".
*
(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Functions of the Target Grammatical Structures in Use
Use of the Past Progressive Tense: Describing an action or other actions that are in progress in the past. Use of The Simple Past Tense vs Past Progressive Tense: Contrasting a completed action at specified time in the past with an action in progress at an exact moment in the past.
Use of Question Tags for The Simple Past Tense & The Past Progressive Tense: Confirming or clarifying past events.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
I need to pop to the market!
This city is full of cool sights!
Let’s catch the bus!
What a traffic jam!
The Topkapı Palace is a must-see in İstanbul!”
Target Phonological Sounds in Use
Vowel: o: (/əʊ/, /ɒ/, /əʊ/)
Consonants: m (/ɛm/,/m/); n: (/ɛn/, /n/); p: ( /piː//p/)
*
(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme.)"

Okul temelli planlama; zümre öğretmenler kurulu tarafından ders kapsamında gerçekleştirilmesi kararlaştırılan araştırma ve gözlem, sosyal etkinlikler, proje çalışmaları, yerel çalışmalar, okuma çalışmaları vb. çalışmaları kapsamaktadır.
