EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
"PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students conduct an interview with a person from their neighbourhood such as a driver, a chemist, a neighbour, an officer etc. about past experiences of these people in the city in terms of public transportation, the pros and cons of different types of transportation in the neighbourhood and city, getting help from services in the neighbourhood and the city and social life. Students begin by preparing interview questions. Next, they elicit and decide the questions. Then, they choose the person for the interview. They may use avatars or AI to create characters for the interviews. The interview should include creative elements, such as charts, or videos, and students will present their findings in class. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme. "
EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
Expansion
Objective:
To talk about activities, services, and transportation options in the city and neighbourhood by listing pros and cons in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity 1: City Life
Discussions The teacher divides the class into three groups with specific topics: Group 1: Activities in attractions and recreational places (e.g., cafés, cinemas, gyms). Group 2: Getting help from services in the neighbourhood and city (e.g., pharmacies, hospitals). Group 3: Pros and cons of different types of transportation in the neighbourhood and city. Each group creates a list of pros and cons using the target vocabulary (e.g., ''Public transport saves time but is often crowded'', or ''Chatting with friends at a café feels relaxing but can be expensive''). Groups present their ideas to the class, and other students ask questions such as, ''Why do you think it is reliable?'' or ''Isn’t it time-consuming?'' After the discussion, each student writes a short paragraph and explains if s/he agrees or disagrees with one idea and why. The teacher provides feedback on accuracy, use of target vocabulary, and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
Supporting
Objective:
To describe past activities in different places in English by using target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity 1: What Were We Doing?
The teacher writes some target words on the board for different places: At the café: drinking tea, chatting with friends. At the gym: lifting weights, doing pilates. At the cinema: watching a movie, eating popcorn. The teacher gives an example and writes it on the board: ''I was drinking tea at the cafe''. Then, students come to the board one by one and write their own sentences (e.g., ''We were watching a movie at the cinema''.). Next, the teacher writes a question and answer on the board: ''What were you doing at the cafe?'' ''I was chatting with friends''. Students practise asking and answering questions in a chain drill game format: one student asks the next, and so on. The teacher gives constructive and supportive feedback on accuracy and pronunciation. Students 340 THE ENGLISH LANGUAGE CURRICULUM reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

plan.KONU:
Sub-themes: ''Continents, countries, and nationalities; shopping for food and personal food preferences; food and food culture from different parts of the world''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Vocabulary for countries and nationalities
Countries (revisional): Türkiye, (UK) United Kingdom (England, Scotland, Wales, Northen Ireland), France, Azerbaijan, Germany, Greece, Italy, Spain, China, Japan, Russia, India.
Nationalities (revisional): Turkish, British (English, Scottish, Welsh, Irish), French, Azerbaijani/Azeri, German, Greek, Italian, Spanish, Chinese, Japanese, Russian, Indian
Vocabulary for countries and nationalities
Countries: Belgium, Croatia, Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Finland, Hungary, the Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Sweden, Switzerland, Egypt, Brazil, Argentina
Nationalities: Belgian, Croatian, Turkish Cypriot, Czech, Danish, Finnish, Hungarian, Dutch, Polish, Portuguese, Swedish, Swiss, Egyptian, Brazilian, Argentinian.
Vocabulary for continents: Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe, Australia, Oceans (The Pacific, Atlantic, Arctic, Indian, Southern). Verbs: to be surrounded.
Vocabulary for shopping for food and personal food preferences
For shopping: A vegetarian, a vegan, a cashier, a shelf, a shop (store-AmE), a trolley (a cart-AmE), a receipt, a discount, a snack, a main course, a starter (an appetizer-AmE), traditional dishes, local dishes.
For preferences
Healthy Food: Nouns: Garlic, grapes, mushroom. Unhealthy Food: Nouns: A burger, a biscuit (cookie-AmE), cereal, a dessert, French fries. Adjectives: Spicy, salty, bitter, sour, savoury (savory- AmE), fried, baked, grilled, gluten-free, dairy-free, sugar-free, halal, delicious, home-made.
Vocabulary for Food and Food culture from different parts of the world:
Nouns: Kebab, baklava (Türkiye), pasta, pizza, steak, falafel (Asian), sushi, chopsticks (Japan), croissant, chopsticks (French).
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, "Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)", "Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)".
*
(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
The Present Perfect Tense (With how long, since, for, already, just) (How long have you been gluten-free? I have been gluten-free since I was sixteen.) (I have been to Ireland for six years. I have already ordered fast food. I have just bought some mushrooms.)
-
Question Tags: (Türkiye is famous for its traditional dishes, isn’t it?) (You’ve eaten sushi before, haven’t you?)
-
“Be able to” (Present, Past, Future, Perfect) (She is able to cook traditional dishes from Türkiye. They were able to find the shop despite the heavy rain. We will be able to buy the ingredients for the recipe tomorrow. I have been able to visit many countries this year.)
-
Countable and Uncountable Nouns (Some, any, much, many): (She bought some vegetables from the market. Do you have any idea where the shop is? How much time do we have left? How many friends do you have in this city?)
-
Need, needn’t for obligation (We need to buy some vegetables for dinner. She needn’t worry about the project, it’s already finished.)
Functions of the Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Use of the Present Perfect Tense: Describing actions that began in the past and continue into the present and describing an action that happened recently and has an impact on the present.
-
Use of the “Question Tags”: Confirming information, encouraging agreement, seeking reassurance.
-
Use of Countable Nouns and Uncountable Nouns: Describing an unspecified amount and uncertainty or absence, and expressing large quantities.
-
Use of Modals “Need, Needn’t” for obligation: Describing that something is required or necessary or is not necessary or obligatory.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
Do you want to grab a bite?
I’ll pick up a salad!
Let’s eat out tonight!
I’m not into spicy food!
Could you lend a hand for this?
Target Phonological Sounds in Use
Consonants: q: /kjuː/, r: /ɑː/(Br), /r/ (AmE); , s: (/s/, /ɛs/, /z/); t : (/tiː/, /t/). *(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme.).

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students prepare a project titled "Global Food Culture and Preferences", focusing on the themes of continents, countries, and nationalities; shopping for food and personal food preferences; and food culture from different parts of the world. First, they research continents, countries, and nationalities, describing their unique features. Then, they explore how people shop for food, talk about personal preferences like vegan, halal, or gluten-free, and highlight traditional and modern dishes. Finally, they look at foods from different cultures, such as sushi, baklava, and pizza, and discuss healthy and unhealthy eating habits. They should use creative elements such as maps, charts, or videos and present their projects in class. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.
EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
Expansion
Objective:
To talk about international foods, their countries of origin, and types through collaborative discussion and critical thinking by using the target vocabulary.
Activity : Food Detective Challenge
The teacher explains that students play a game as ''Food Detectives'' to solve a mystery about three international dishes. The teacher plays an audio or reads a script with clues about the foods, such as their country of origin, type (e.g., dessert, main course), and cultural significance. Students listen carefully and fill out a worksheet with the following details: Food Name: Country of Origin: Type of Dish (Dessert/Main Course/Snack): Next, they work in groups to compare answers. Then, each group creates a new clue for a different food and exchanges it with another group to solve. The teacher gives constructive and supportive feedback on accuracy and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
Supporting
Objective:
To talk about popular international food items and their countries of origin in English by using target vocabulary.
Activity : Exploring Food Cultures Around the World
The teacher begins the lesson by showing students pictures of popular international foods (e.g., pizza, sushi, baklava, tacos, croissants) and asking if they know where these foods come from or if they have tried them. The teacher provides a list of foods and their countries of origin, then writes example sentences on the board, such as ''Pizza is from Italy'', or ''Baklava is a traditional Turkish dessert''. Students write their own sentences following this structure. Each student then chooses a favourite food from another culture, draws it, and labels it with a sentence such as ''Tacos are from Mexico''. Finally, students present their drawings to the class, explaining what the food is, where it is from, and why they like it. The teacher gives constructive and supportive feedback on accuracy and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

plan.KONU:
Sub-themes: ''Continents, countries, and nationalities; shopping for food and personal food preferences; food and food culture from different parts of the world''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Vocabulary for countries and nationalities
Countries (revisional): Türkiye, (UK) United Kingdom (England, Scotland, Wales, Northen Ireland), France, Azerbaijan, Germany, Greece, Italy, Spain, China, Japan, Russia, India.
Nationalities (revisional): Turkish, British (English, Scottish, Welsh, Irish), French, Azerbaijani/Azeri, German, Greek, Italian, Spanish, Chinese, Japanese, Russian, Indian
Vocabulary for countries and nationalities
Countries: Belgium, Croatia, Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Finland, Hungary, the Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Sweden, Switzerland, Egypt, Brazil, Argentina
Nationalities: Belgian, Croatian, Turkish Cypriot, Czech, Danish, Finnish, Hungarian, Dutch, Polish, Portuguese, Swedish, Swiss, Egyptian, Brazilian, Argentinian.
Vocabulary for continents: Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe, Australia, Oceans (The Pacific, Atlantic, Arctic, Indian, Southern). Verbs: to be surrounded.
Vocabulary for shopping for food and personal food preferences
For shopping: A vegetarian, a vegan, a cashier, a shelf, a shop (store-AmE), a trolley (a cart-AmE), a receipt, a discount, a snack, a main course, a starter (an appetizer-AmE), traditional dishes, local dishes.
For preferences
Healthy Food: Nouns: Garlic, grapes, mushroom. Unhealthy Food: Nouns: A burger, a biscuit (cookie-AmE), cereal, a dessert, French fries. Adjectives: Spicy, salty, bitter, sour, savoury (savory- AmE), fried, baked, grilled, gluten-free, dairy-free, sugar-free, halal, delicious, home-made.
Vocabulary for Food and Food culture from different parts of the world:
Nouns: Kebab, baklava (Türkiye), pasta, pizza, steak, falafel (Asian), sushi, chopsticks (Japan), croissant, chopsticks (French).
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, "Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)", "Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)".
*
(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
The Present Perfect Tense (With how long, since, for, already, just) (How long have you been gluten-free? I have been gluten-free since I was sixteen.) (I have been to Ireland for six years. I have already ordered fast food. I have just bought some mushrooms.)
-
Question Tags: (Türkiye is famous for its traditional dishes, isn’t it?) (You’ve eaten sushi before, haven’t you?)
-
“Be able to” (Present, Past, Future, Perfect) (She is able to cook traditional dishes from Türkiye. They were able to find the shop despite the heavy rain. We will be able to buy the ingredients for the recipe tomorrow. I have been able to visit many countries this year.)
-
Countable and Uncountable Nouns (Some, any, much, many): (She bought some vegetables from the market. Do you have any idea where the shop is? How much time do we have left? How many friends do you have in this city?)
-
Need, needn’t for obligation (We need to buy some vegetables for dinner. She needn’t worry about the project, it’s already finished.)
Functions of the Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Use of the Present Perfect Tense: Describing actions that began in the past and continue into the present and describing an action that happened recently and has an impact on the present.
-
Use of the “Question Tags”: Confirming information, encouraging agreement, seeking reassurance.
-
Use of Countable Nouns and Uncountable Nouns: Describing an unspecified amount and uncertainty or absence, and expressing large quantities.
-
Use of Modals “Need, Needn’t” for obligation: Describing that something is required or necessary or is not necessary or obligatory.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
Do you want to grab a bite?
I’ll pick up a salad!
Let’s eat out tonight!
I’m not into spicy food!
Could you lend a hand for this?
Target Phonological Sounds in Use
Consonants: q: /kjuː/, r: /ɑː/(Br), /r/ (AmE); , s: (/s/, /ɛs/, /z/); t : (/tiː/, /t/). *(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme.).

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students prepare a project titled "Global Food Culture and Preferences", focusing on the themes of continents, countries, and nationalities; shopping for food and personal food preferences; and food culture from different parts of the world. First, they research continents, countries, and nationalities, describing their unique features. Then, they explore how people shop for food, talk about personal preferences like vegan, halal, or gluten-free, and highlight traditional and modern dishes. Finally, they look at foods from different cultures, such as sushi, baklava, and pizza, and discuss healthy and unhealthy eating habits. They should use creative elements such as maps, charts, or videos and present their projects in class. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.
EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
Expansion
Objective:
To talk about international foods, their countries of origin, and types through collaborative discussion and critical thinking by using the target vocabulary.
Activity : Food Detective Challenge
The teacher explains that students play a game as ''Food Detectives'' to solve a mystery about three international dishes. The teacher plays an audio or reads a script with clues about the foods, such as their country of origin, type (e.g., dessert, main course), and cultural significance. Students listen carefully and fill out a worksheet with the following details: Food Name: Country of Origin: Type of Dish (Dessert/Main Course/Snack): Next, they work in groups to compare answers. Then, each group creates a new clue for a different food and exchanges it with another group to solve. The teacher gives constructive and supportive feedback on accuracy and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
Supporting
Objective:
To talk about popular international food items and their countries of origin in English by using target vocabulary.
Activity : Exploring Food Cultures Around the World
The teacher begins the lesson by showing students pictures of popular international foods (e.g., pizza, sushi, baklava, tacos, croissants) and asking if they know where these foods come from or if they have tried them. The teacher provides a list of foods and their countries of origin, then writes example sentences on the board, such as ''Pizza is from Italy'', or ''Baklava is a traditional Turkish dessert''. Students write their own sentences following this structure. Each student then chooses a favourite food from another culture, draws it, and labels it with a sentence such as ''Tacos are from Mexico''. Finally, students present their drawings to the class, explaining what the food is, where it is from, and why they like it. The teacher gives constructive and supportive feedback on accuracy and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

plan.KONU:
Sub-themes: ''Continents, countries, and nationalities; shopping for food and personal food preferences; food and food culture from different parts of the world''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Vocabulary for countries and nationalities
Countries (revisional): Türkiye, (UK) United Kingdom (England, Scotland, Wales, Northen Ireland), France, Azerbaijan, Germany, Greece, Italy, Spain, China, Japan, Russia, India.
Nationalities (revisional): Turkish, British (English, Scottish, Welsh, Irish), French, Azerbaijani/Azeri, German, Greek, Italian, Spanish, Chinese, Japanese, Russian, Indian
Vocabulary for countries and nationalities
Countries: Belgium, Croatia, Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Finland, Hungary, the Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Sweden, Switzerland, Egypt, Brazil, Argentina
Nationalities: Belgian, Croatian, Turkish Cypriot, Czech, Danish, Finnish, Hungarian, Dutch, Polish, Portuguese, Swedish, Swiss, Egyptian, Brazilian, Argentinian.
Vocabulary for continents: Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe, Australia, Oceans (The Pacific, Atlantic, Arctic, Indian, Southern). Verbs: to be surrounded.
Vocabulary for shopping for food and personal food preferences
For shopping: A vegetarian, a vegan, a cashier, a shelf, a shop (store-AmE), a trolley (a cart-AmE), a receipt, a discount, a snack, a main course, a starter (an appetizer-AmE), traditional dishes, local dishes.
For preferences
Healthy Food: Nouns: Garlic, grapes, mushroom. Unhealthy Food: Nouns: A burger, a biscuit (cookie-AmE), cereal, a dessert, French fries. Adjectives: Spicy, salty, bitter, sour, savoury (savory- AmE), fried, baked, grilled, gluten-free, dairy-free, sugar-free, halal, delicious, home-made.
Vocabulary for Food and Food culture from different parts of the world:
Nouns: Kebab, baklava (Türkiye), pasta, pizza, steak, falafel (Asian), sushi, chopsticks (Japan), croissant, chopsticks (French).
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, "Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)", "Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)".
*
(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
The Present Perfect Tense (With how long, since, for, already, just) (How long have you been gluten-free? I have been gluten-free since I was sixteen.) (I have been to Ireland for six years. I have already ordered fast food. I have just bought some mushrooms.)
-
Question Tags: (Türkiye is famous for its traditional dishes, isn’t it?) (You’ve eaten sushi before, haven’t you?)
-
“Be able to” (Present, Past, Future, Perfect) (She is able to cook traditional dishes from Türkiye. They were able to find the shop despite the heavy rain. We will be able to buy the ingredients for the recipe tomorrow. I have been able to visit many countries this year.)
-
Countable and Uncountable Nouns (Some, any, much, many): (She bought some vegetables from the market. Do you have any idea where the shop is? How much time do we have left? How many friends do you have in this city?)
-
Need, needn’t for obligation (We need to buy some vegetables for dinner. She needn’t worry about the project, it’s already finished.)
Functions of the Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Use of the Present Perfect Tense: Describing actions that began in the past and continue into the present and describing an action that happened recently and has an impact on the present.
-
Use of the “Question Tags”: Confirming information, encouraging agreement, seeking reassurance.
-
Use of Countable Nouns and Uncountable Nouns: Describing an unspecified amount and uncertainty or absence, and expressing large quantities.
-
Use of Modals “Need, Needn’t” for obligation: Describing that something is required or necessary or is not necessary or obligatory.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
Do you want to grab a bite?
I’ll pick up a salad!
Let’s eat out tonight!
I’m not into spicy food!
Could you lend a hand for this?
Target Phonological Sounds in Use
Consonants: q: /kjuː/, r: /ɑː/(Br), /r/ (AmE); , s: (/s/, /ɛs/, /z/); t : (/tiː/, /t/). *(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme.).

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students prepare a project titled "Global Food Culture and Preferences", focusing on the themes of continents, countries, and nationalities; shopping for food and personal food preferences; and food culture from different parts of the world. First, they research continents, countries, and nationalities, describing their unique features. Then, they explore how people shop for food, talk about personal preferences like vegan, halal, or gluten-free, and highlight traditional and modern dishes. Finally, they look at foods from different cultures, such as sushi, baklava, and pizza, and discuss healthy and unhealthy eating habits. They should use creative elements such as maps, charts, or videos and present their projects in class. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.
EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
Expansion
Objective:
To talk about international foods, their countries of origin, and types through collaborative discussion and critical thinking by using the target vocabulary.
Activity : Food Detective Challenge
The teacher explains that students play a game as ''Food Detectives'' to solve a mystery about three international dishes. The teacher plays an audio or reads a script with clues about the foods, such as their country of origin, type (e.g., dessert, main course), and cultural significance. Students listen carefully and fill out a worksheet with the following details: Food Name: Country of Origin: Type of Dish (Dessert/Main Course/Snack): Next, they work in groups to compare answers. Then, each group creates a new clue for a different food and exchanges it with another group to solve. The teacher gives constructive and supportive feedback on accuracy and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
Supporting
Objective:
To talk about popular international food items and their countries of origin in English by using target vocabulary.
Activity : Exploring Food Cultures Around the World
The teacher begins the lesson by showing students pictures of popular international foods (e.g., pizza, sushi, baklava, tacos, croissants) and asking if they know where these foods come from or if they have tried them. The teacher provides a list of foods and their countries of origin, then writes example sentences on the board, such as ''Pizza is from Italy'', or ''Baklava is a traditional Turkish dessert''. Students write their own sentences following this structure. Each student then chooses a favourite food from another culture, draws it, and labels it with a sentence such as ''Tacos are from Mexico''. Finally, students present their drawings to the class, explaining what the food is, where it is from, and why they like it. The teacher gives constructive and supportive feedback on accuracy and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

Sub-themes: ''Continents, countries, and nationalities; shopping for food and personal food preferences; food and food culture from different parts of the world''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Vocabulary for countries and nationalities
Countries (revisional): Türkiye, (UK) United Kingdom (England, Scotland, Wales, Northen Ireland), France, Azerbaijan, Germany, Greece, Italy, Spain, China, Japan, Russia, India.
Nationalities (revisional): Turkish, British (English, Scottish, Welsh, Irish), French, Azerbaijani/Azeri, German, Greek, Italian, Spanish, Chinese, Japanese, Russian, Indian
Vocabulary for countries and nationalities
Countries: Belgium, Croatia, Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Finland, Hungary, the Netherlands, Poland, Portugal, Sweden, Switzerland, Egypt, Brazil, Argentina
Nationalities: Belgian, Croatian, Turkish Cypriot, Czech, Danish, Finnish, Hungarian, Dutch, Polish, Portuguese, Swedish, Swiss, Egyptian, Brazilian, Argentinian.
Vocabulary for continents: Asia, Africa, North America, South America, Antarctica, Europe, Australia, Oceans (The Pacific, Atlantic, Arctic, Indian, Southern). Verbs: to be surrounded.
Vocabulary for shopping for food and personal food preferences
For shopping: A vegetarian, a vegan, a cashier, a shelf, a shop (store-AmE), a trolley (a cart-AmE), a receipt, a discount, a snack, a main course, a starter (an appetizer-AmE), traditional dishes, local dishes.
For preferences
Healthy Food: Nouns: Garlic, grapes, mushroom. Unhealthy Food: Nouns: A burger, a biscuit (cookie-AmE), cereal, a dessert, French fries. Adjectives: Spicy, salty, bitter, sour, savoury (savory- AmE), fried, baked, grilled, gluten-free, dairy-free, sugar-free, halal, delicious, home-made.
Vocabulary for Food and Food culture from different parts of the world:
Nouns: Kebab, baklava (Türkiye), pasta, pizza, steak, falafel (Asian), sushi, chopsticks (Japan), croissant, chopsticks (French).
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, "Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)", "Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)".
*
(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
The Present Perfect Tense (With how long, since, for, already, just) (How long have you been gluten-free? I have been gluten-free since I was sixteen.) (I have been to Ireland for six years. I have already ordered fast food. I have just bought some mushrooms.)
-
Question Tags: (Türkiye is famous for its traditional dishes, isn’t it?) (You’ve eaten sushi before, haven’t you?)
-
“Be able to” (Present, Past, Future, Perfect) (She is able to cook traditional dishes from Türkiye. They were able to find the shop despite the heavy rain. We will be able to buy the ingredients for the recipe tomorrow. I have been able to visit many countries this year.)
-
Countable and Uncountable Nouns (Some, any, much, many): (She bought some vegetables from the market. Do you have any idea where the shop is? How much time do we have left? How many friends do you have in this city?)
-
Need, needn’t for obligation (We need to buy some vegetables for dinner. She needn’t worry about the project, it’s already finished.)
Functions of the Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Use of the Present Perfect Tense: Describing actions that began in the past and continue into the present and describing an action that happened recently and has an impact on the present.
-
Use of the “Question Tags”: Confirming information, encouraging agreement, seeking reassurance.
-
Use of Countable Nouns and Uncountable Nouns: Describing an unspecified amount and uncertainty or absence, and expressing large quantities.
-
Use of Modals “Need, Needn’t” for obligation: Describing that something is required or necessary or is not necessary or obligatory.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
Do you want to grab a bite?
I’ll pick up a salad!
Let’s eat out tonight!
I’m not into spicy food!
Could you lend a hand for this?
Target Phonological Sounds in Use
Consonants: q: /kjuː/, r: /ɑː/(Br), /r/ (AmE); , s: (/s/, /ɛs/, /z/); t : (/tiː/, /t/). *(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme.).

Vocabulary for global problems related to natural resources
Nouns: Deforestation, soil pollution, habitat destruction, global warming, climate change, landslides, floods, loss of biodiversity, energy crisis, water shortage, overpopulation, urbanisation, industrialisation, poverty, carbon footprint, greenhouse gases, environmental problems.
Vocabulary for protecting natural resources
Verbs: To use energy efficiently, to reduce consumption, to be environmentally conscious, to raise awareness, to take precautions, to reuse, to limit.

-
Defining Relative Clauses (that, which, who): (Renewable resources which include solar and wind energy are necessary for sustainable development.)
-
Connecting Words (so…): (People need to take precautions, so they can protect wildlife from habitat destruction.)
-
Use of Defining Relative clauses (that, which, who): Referring to people, objects or thingsto provide essential information.
-
Use of connecting words (so…): Expressing cause and effect; explaining consequences.
People need to take care of Mother nature’s bounty!

EK_ALANLAR.Okul Temelli Planlama:
Okul temelli planlama; zümre öğretmenler kurulu tarafından ders kapsamında gerçekleştirilmesi kararlaştırılan araştırma ve gözlem, sosyal etkinlikler, proje çalışmaları, yerel çalışmalar, okuma çalışmaları vb. çalışmaları kapsamaktadır. Çalışmalar için ayrılan süre eğitim-öğretim yılı içinde planlanır ve yıllık planlarda ifade edilir.
Bu planlamalar kapsamında yürütülecek öğretim faaliyetleri; öğrenci katılımını desteklemeli, yaparak ve yaşayarak öğrenmeye olanak tanımalı, öğrencinin bütüncül gelişime hizmet etmelidir. *Bu çerçeve planda belirtilen okul temelli planlama haftaları örnek olarak sunulmuştur. Zümre öğretmenler kurulunda aldığınız karara göre okul ve ders koşullarınıza uygun (öğretim programında belirtilen okul temelli planlama ders saati 2 haftadan fazla sürebilir) düzenleyebilirsiniz.

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students prepare a project titled "Global Food Culture and Preferences", focusing on the themes of continents, countries, and nationalities; shopping for food and personal food preferences; and food culture from different parts of the world. First, they research continents, countries, and nationalities, describing their unique features. Then, they explore how people shop for food, talk about personal preferences like vegan, halal, or gluten-free, and highlight traditional and modern dishes. Finally, they look at foods from different cultures, such as sushi, baklava, and pizza, and discuss healthy and unhealthy eating habits. They should use creative elements such as maps, charts, or videos and present their projects in class. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
They design and present a project that explores the challenges and solutions related to natural resources (e.g. water, air); global problems related to natural resources; protecting natural resources. They research the importance of conserving natural resources and protecting natural resources, analyse the effects of human activity on nature, and propose actionable steps for a more sustainable future. As part of the project, students write reports, create visual aids (such as posters or presentations), and role- play as conservationists, scientists, or environmental activists. They will simulate scenarios like addressing global problems related to natural resources, pollution, or raising awareness about sustainable practices. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.
EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
Expansion
Objective:
To talk about international foods, their countries of origin, and types through collaborative discussion and critical thinking by using the target vocabulary.
Activity : Food Detective Challenge
The teacher explains that students play a game as ''Food Detectives'' to solve a mystery about three international dishes. The teacher plays an audio or reads a script with clues about the foods, such as their country of origin, type (e.g., dessert, main course), and cultural significance. Students listen carefully and fill out a worksheet with the following details: Food Name: Country of Origin: Type of Dish (Dessert/Main Course/Snack): Next, they work in groups to compare answers. Then, each group creates a new clue for a different food and exchanges it with another group to solve. The teacher gives constructive and supportive feedback on accuracy and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
Supporting
Objective:
To talk about popular international food items and their countries of origin in English by using target vocabulary.
Activity : Exploring Food Cultures Around the World
The teacher begins the lesson by showing students pictures of popular international foods (e.g., pizza, sushi, baklava, tacos, croissants) and asking if they know where these foods come from or if they have tried them. The teacher provides a list of foods and their countries of origin, then writes example sentences on the board, such as ''Pizza is from Italy'', or ''Baklava is a traditional Turkish dessert''. Students write their own sentences following this structure. Each student then chooses a favourite food from another culture, draws it, and labels it with a sentence such as ''Tacos are from Mexico''. Finally, students present their drawings to the class, explaining what the food is, where it is from, and why they like it. The teacher gives constructive and supportive feedback on accuracy and pronunciation. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
Objective: To talk about global problems related to natural resources and solutions by using the target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Solutions for Global Problems
The teacher divides students into small groups and assigns each group a global problem, such as climate change or water shortage. Students discuss the problem using the target vocabulary, including terms such as ''renewable resources'', ''efficient energy use'', ''to recycle'', and ''to raise awareness'', as well as structures such as ''which, that, and so''. Each group creates a plan that explains the problem, its causes, and solutions with reasons. For example, for climate change, a group might state: ''Climate change, which is caused by greenhouse gases and overuse of fossil fuels, requires immediate action. We suggest using renewable resources, such as solar and wind energy, that are sustainable and reduce carbon emissions. To solve this, it is important to raise awareness, so people learn to save energy and recycle''. After each group presentation, the teacher provides feedback on correct use of target vocabulary and target grammar. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
Objective: To identify and categorise natural resources, global problems, and actions to protect the environment in English by using the target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Save the Planet: Match and Share
The teacher shows flashcards of natural resources such as water, forests, and animals, asks students to name them, and repeats the words. Next, s/he provides a worksheet with vocabulary words like ''solar energy'', ''pollution'', and ''to recycle'' and asks students to match them to the categories ''Natural Resources'', ''Global Problems'', and ''Protecting Natural Resources'' by drawing lines. For example, students will match ''solar energy'' to ''Natural Resources'', ''Pollution'' to ''Global Problems'', and ''To recycle'' to ''Protecting Natural Resources''. After completing the worksheet, students take turns reading aloud the words they matched in each category. The teacher listens, provides feedback, and corrects any misplacements. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

plan.ÜNİTE:
THEME 7: LIFE IN NATURE & GLOBAL
PROBLEMS
plan.KONU:
Sub-themes: ''Natural resources; global problems related to natural resources; protecting natural resources''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Vocabulary for natural resources
Nouns: Renewable resources, non-renewable resources, solar energy, wind energy, geothermal energy, freshwater, groundwater.
Vocabulary for global problems related to natural resources
Nouns: Deforestation, soil pollution, habitat destruction, global warming, climate change, landslides, floods, loss of biodiversity, energy crisis, water shortage, overpopulation, urbanisation, industrialisation, poverty, carbon footprint, greenhouse gases, environmental problems.
Vocabulary for protecting natural resources
Verbs: To use energy efficiently, to reduce consumption, to be environmentally conscious, to raise awareness, to take precautions, to reuse, to limit.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, "Eid alFitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)", "Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)".
*
(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Defining Relative Clauses (that, which, who): (Renewable resources which include solar and wind energy are necessary for sustainable development.)
-
Connecting Words (so…): (People need to take precautions, so they can protect wildlife from habitat destruction.)
Functions of the Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Use of Defining Relative clauses (that, which, who): Referring to people, objects or thingsto provide essential information.
-
Use of connecting words (so…): Expressing cause and effect; explaining consequences.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
People need to take care of Mother nature’s bounty!
Our planet works like a well-oiled machine!
We’re at the tipping point with the loss of our ecosystem!
Let’s save our planet!
Let’s be green thumbs and plant trees!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use
Vowel: u: (/juː/, /ʌ/, /juː/)
Consonants: v: (/viː/, /v/); w: (/w/)
*
(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme.)

EK_ALANLAR.Okul Temelli Planlama:
Okul temelli planlama; zümre öğretmenler kurulu tarafından ders kapsamında gerçekleştirilmesi kararlaştırılan araştırma ve gözlem, sosyal etkinlikler, proje çalışmaları, yerel çalışmalar, okuma çalışmaları vb. çalışmaları kapsamaktadır. Çalışmalar için ayrılan süre eğitim-öğretim yılı içinde planlanır ve yıllık planlarda ifade edilir.
Bu planlamalar kapsamında yürütülecek öğretim faaliyetleri; öğrenci katılımını desteklemeli, yaparak ve yaşayarak öğrenmeye olanak tanımalı, öğrencinin bütüncül gelişime hizmet etmelidir. *Bu çerçeve planda belirtilen okul temelli planlama haftaları örnek olarak sunulmuştur. Zümre öğretmenler kurulunda aldığınız karara göre okul ve ders koşullarınıza uygun (öğretim programında belirtilen okul temelli planlama ders saati 2 haftadan fazla sürebilir) düzenleyebilirsiniz.

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
They design and present a project that explores the challenges and solutions related to natural resources (e.g. water, air); global problems related to natural resources; protecting natural resources. They research the importance of conserving natural resources and protecting natural resources, analyse the effects of human activity on nature, and propose actionable steps for a more sustainable future. As part of the project, students write reports, create visual aids (such as posters or presentations), and role- play as conservationists, scientists, or environmental activists. They will simulate scenarios like addressing global problems related to natural resources, pollution, or raising awareness about sustainable practices. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.
EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
Expansion
Objective: To talk about global problems related to natural resources and solutions by using the target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Solutions for Global Problems
The teacher divides students into small groups and assigns each group a global problem, such as climate change or water shortage. Students discuss the problem using the target vocabulary, including terms such as ''renewable resources'', ''efficient energy use'', ''to recycle'', and ''to raise awareness'', as well as structures such as ''which, that, and so''. Each group creates a plan that explains the problem, its causes, and solutions with reasons. For example, for climate change, a group might state: ''Climate change, which is caused by greenhouse gases and overuse of fossil fuels, requires immediate action. We suggest using renewable resources, such as solar and wind energy, that are sustainable and reduce carbon emissions. To solve this, it is important to raise awareness, so people learn to save energy and recycle''. After each group presentation, the teacher provides feedback on correct use of target vocabulary and target grammar. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
Supporting
Objective: To identify and categorise natural resources, global problems, and actions to protect the environment in English by using the target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Save the Planet: Match and Share
The teacher shows flashcards of natural resources such as water, forests, and animals, asks students to name them, and repeats the words. Next, s/he provides a worksheet with vocabulary words like ''solar energy'', ''pollution'', and ''to recycle'' and asks students to match them to the categories ''Natural Resources'', ''Global Problems'', and ''Protecting Natural Resources'' by drawing lines. For example, students will match ''solar energy'' to ''Natural Resources'', ''Pollution'' to ''Global Problems'', and ''To recycle'' to ''Protecting Natural Resources''. After completing the worksheet, students take turns reading aloud the words they matched in each category. The teacher listens, provides feedback, and corrects any misplacements. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

plan.KONU:
Sub-themes: ''Natural resources; global problems related to natural resources; protecting natural resources''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Vocabulary for natural resources
Nouns: Renewable resources, non-renewable resources, solar energy, wind energy, geothermal energy, freshwater, groundwater.
Vocabulary for global problems related to natural resources
Nouns: Deforestation, soil pollution, habitat destruction, global warming, climate change, landslides, floods, loss of biodiversity, energy crisis, water shortage, overpopulation, urbanisation, industrialisation, poverty, carbon footprint, greenhouse gases, environmental problems.
Vocabulary for protecting natural resources
Verbs: To use energy efficiently, to reduce consumption, to be environmentally conscious, to raise awareness, to take precautions, to reuse, to limit.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, "Eid alFitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)", "Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)".
*
(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Defining Relative Clauses (that, which, who): (Renewable resources which include solar and wind energy are necessary for sustainable development.)
-
Connecting Words (so…): (People need to take precautions, so they can protect wildlife from habitat destruction.)
Functions of the Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Use of Defining Relative clauses (that, which, who): Referring to people, objects or thingsto provide essential information.
-
Use of connecting words (so…): Expressing cause and effect; explaining consequences.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
People need to take care of Mother nature’s bounty!
Our planet works like a well-oiled machine!
We’re at the tipping point with the loss of our ecosystem!
Let’s save our planet!
Let’s be green thumbs and plant trees!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use
Vowel: u: (/juː/, /ʌ/, /juː/)
Consonants: v: (/viː/, /v/); w: (/w/)
*
(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme.)

They will simulate scenarios like addressing global problems related to natural resources, pollution, or raising awareness about sustainable practices. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.
EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
Expansion
Objective: To talk about global problems related to natural resources and solutions by using the target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Solutions for Global Problems
The teacher divides students into small groups and assigns each group a global problem, such as climate change or water shortage. Students discuss the problem using the target vocabulary, including terms such as ''renewable resources'', ''efficient energy use'', ''to recycle'', and ''to raise awareness'', as well as structures such as ''which, that, and so''. Each group creates a plan that explains the problem, its causes, and solutions with reasons. For example, for climate change, a group might state: ''Climate change, which is caused by greenhouse gases and overuse of fossil fuels, requires immediate action. We suggest using renewable resources, such as solar and wind energy, that are sustainable and reduce carbon emissions. To solve this, it is important to raise awareness, so people learn to save energy and recycle''. After each group presentation, the teacher provides feedback on correct use of target vocabulary and target grammar. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
Supporting
Objective: To identify and categorise natural resources, global problems, and actions to protect the environment in English by using the target vocabulary.
Activity 1: Save the Planet: Match and Share
The teacher shows flashcards of natural resources such as water, forests, and animals, asks students to name them, and repeats the words. Next, s/he provides a worksheet with vocabulary words like ''solar energy'', ''pollution'', and ''to recycle'' and asks students to match them to the categories ''Natural Resources'', ''Global Problems'', and ''Protecting Natural Resources'' by drawing lines. For example, students will match ''solar energy'' to ''Natural Resources'', ''Pollution'' to ''Global Problems'', and ''To recycle'' to ''Protecting Natural Resources''. After completing the worksheet, students take turns reading aloud the words they matched in each category. The teacher listens, provides feedback, and corrects any misplacements. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

THEME 7: LIFE IN NATURE & GLOBAL
PROBLEMS
plan.KONU:
Sub-themes: ''Natural resources; global problems related to natural resources; protecting natural resources''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Vocabulary for natural resources
Nouns: Renewable resources, non-renewable resources, solar energy, wind energy, geothermal energy, freshwater, groundwater.
Vocabulary for global problems related to natural resources
Nouns: Deforestation, soil pollution, habitat destruction, global warming, climate change, landslides, floods, loss of biodiversity, energy crisis, water shortage, overpopulation, urbanisation, industrialisation, poverty, carbon footprint, greenhouse gases, environmental problems.
Vocabulary for protecting natural resources
Verbs: To use energy efficiently, to reduce consumption, to be environmentally conscious, to raise awareness, to take precautions, to reuse, to limit.
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, "Eid alFitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)", "Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)".
*
(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Defining Relative Clauses (that, which, who): (Renewable resources which include solar and wind energy are necessary for sustainable development.)
-
Connecting Words (so…): (People need to take precautions, so they can protect wildlife from habitat destruction.)
Functions of the Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Use of Defining Relative clauses (that, which, who): Referring to people, objects or thingsto provide essential information.
-
Use of connecting words (so…): Expressing cause and effect; explaining consequences.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
People need to take care of Mother nature’s bounty!
Our planet works like a well-oiled machine!
We’re at the tipping point with the loss of our ecosystem!
Let’s save our planet!
Let’s be green thumbs and plant trees!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use
Vowel: u: (/juː/, /ʌ/, /juː/)
Consonants: v: (/viː/, /v/); w: (/w/)
*
(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme.)

After completing the worksheet, students take turns reading aloud the words they matched in each category. The teacher listens, provides feedback, and corrects any misplacements. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

plan.KONU:
"Sub-themes: ''Planets and space; life in the universe; space explorations''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Vocabulary for planets and space
Planets: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune. Nouns: Universe, galaxy, Milky Way, solar system, satellite, a meteor, an asteroid, a comet, an orbit, to revolve, Adjective: Celestial.
Vocabulary for life in the universe
Nouns: Atmosphere, a robot, a creature, a space colony, Adjectives: tiny, unknown, weird. mysterious, rare. Vocabulary for space explorations:
Nouns: Space travel, space mission, telescope, an astronaut, a spacecraft, a rocket, a space shuttle, a space capsule Verbs: to launch, to take off, to land, to collect data, to conduct experiments, to go on a spacewalk
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, ""Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)"", ""Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)"".
*
(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Zero Conditional: (If you go to the Moon, everything floats in space. If a planet is in orbit, it travels around a star.)
-
Conditional 1: (If you want to explore space, you can become an astronaut.)
Functions of the Target Grammatical Structures in Use
Use of the Zero Conditional: Describing general and/or scientific facts which are generally true.
Use of the Conditional 1: Describing a possible future situation.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
It’s a small world!
She’s so strange, she is definitely not from this planet!
A star is born!
This is a whole new world!
It felt like being a man on the moon!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use
Consonants: x: (/ɛks/, /ks/, /gz/); y: (/waɪ//waɪ//waɪ/, /j/, /ɪ/, /iː/); z: /zed/ (Br), /ziː/ (AmE), /z/)
*
(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme.)"

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students create a poster which is about life in 2100. They brainstorm about the possibilities in the future such as robots, aliens, space colonies, space travel, etc. Based on these ideas, students produce sentences about their future using the target grammar structures. Also, they add some visuals on their posters. The project could also be designed with the help of web 2.0 tools if students prefer. As a final stage, they present their posters in the classroom and find the common possibilities about the future. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.
EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
Expansion
Objective: To create a futuristic story about planets and space by using target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity 1: Creative Writing: Life in 2124
The teacher explains the task clearly. Students imagine life in the future, such as living on another planet. The teacher gives examples of sentences with target grammar and target vocabulary (e.g., ''If we find new planets, we will need better rockets''.). Next, students write their stories using target grammar and target vocabulary. Then, they read their stories aloud. The teacher listens and gives feedback on pronunciation and sentence correctness. Students reflect on the activity. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
Supporting
Objective: To talk about possible future scenarios in space explorations by using target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity 1: Future Space Possibilities
The teacher begins the activity by showing flashcards with key words from the word bank (e.g., robots, explore, live, discover, build) and explaining their meanings with visuals or simple definitions. Students then pair up and receive a worksheet with the target grammar such as ''If humans colonise Mars, _________________________ '', and ''If we build better rockets, ___________________________ ''. They use the word bank to fill in the blanks (e.g., ''If we build better rockets, we will explore new planets''.). In the end, the teacher provides feedback on pronunciation and accuracy. Students reflect on the activity. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity."

Zero Conditional: (If you go to the Moon, everything floats in space. If a planet is in orbit, it travels around a star.)
-
Conditional 1: (If you want to explore space, you can become an astronaut.)
Functions of the Target Grammatical Structures in Use
Use of the Zero Conditional: Describing general and/or scientific facts which are generally true.
Use of the Conditional 1: Describing a possible future situation.

A star is born!
This is a whole new world!
It felt like being a man on the moon!

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students create a poster which is about life in 2100. They brainstorm about the possibilities in the future such as robots, aliens, space colonies, space travel, etc. Based on these ideas, students produce sentences about their future using the target grammar structures. Also, they add some visuals on their posters. The project could also be designed with the help of web 2.0 tools if students prefer. As a final stage, they present their posters in the classroom and find the common possibilities about the future. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.
EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
Expansion
Objective: To create a futuristic story about planets and space by using target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity 1: Creative Writing: Life in 2124
The teacher explains the task clearly. Students imagine life in the future, such as living on another planet. The teacher gives examples of sentences with target grammar and target vocabulary (e.g., ''If we find new planets, we will need better rockets''.). Next, students write their stories using target grammar and target vocabulary. Then, they read their stories aloud. The teacher listens and gives feedback on pronunciation and sentence correctness. Students reflect on the activity. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
Supporting
Objective: To talk about possible future scenarios in space explorations by using target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity 1: Future Space Possibilities
The teacher begins the activity by showing flashcards with key words from the word bank (e.g., robots, explore, live, discover, build) and explaining their meanings with visuals or simple definitions. Students then pair up and receive a worksheet with the target grammar such as ''If humans colonise Mars, _________________________ '', and ''If we build better rockets, ___________________________ ''. They use the word bank to fill in the blanks (e.g., ''If we build better rockets, we will explore new planets''.). In the end, the teacher provides feedback on pronunciation and accuracy. Students reflect on the activity. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

plan.KONU:
Sub-themes: ''Planets and space; life in the universe; space explorations''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Vocabulary for planets and space
Planets: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune. Nouns: Universe, galaxy, Milky Way, solar system, satellite, a meteor, an asteroid, a comet, an orbit, to revolve, Adjective: Celestial.
Vocabulary for life in the universe
Nouns: Atmosphere, a robot, a creature, a space colony, Adjectives: tiny, unknown, weird. mysterious, rare. Vocabulary for space explorations:
Nouns: Space travel, space mission, telescope, an astronaut, a spacecraft, a rocket, a space shuttle, a space capsule Verbs: to launch, to take off, to land, to collect data, to conduct experiments, to go on a spacewalk
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, "Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)", "Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)".
*
(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Zero Conditional: (If you go to the Moon, everything floats in space. If a planet is in orbit, it travels around a star.)
-
Conditional 1: (If you want to explore space, you can become an astronaut.)
Functions of the Target Grammatical Structures in Use
Use of the Zero Conditional: Describing general and/or scientific facts which are generally true.
Use of the Conditional 1: Describing a possible future situation.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
It’s a small world!
She’s so strange, she is definitely not from this planet!
A star is born!
This is a whole new world!
It felt like being a man on the moon!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use
Consonants: x: (/ɛks/, /ks/, /gz/); y: (/waɪ//waɪ//waɪ/, /j/, /ɪ/, /iː/); z: /zed/ (Br), /ziː/ (AmE), /z/)
*
(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme.)

EK_ALANLAR.Okul Temelli Planlama:
Okul temelli planlama; zümre öğretmenler kurulu tarafından ders kapsamında gerçekleştirilmesi kararlaştırılan araştırma ve gözlem, sosyal etkinlikler, proje çalışmaları, yerel çalışmalar, okuma çalışmaları vb. çalışmaları kapsamaktadır. Çalışmalar için ayrılan süre eğitim-öğretim yılı içinde planlanır ve yıllık planlarda ifade edilir.
Bu planlamalar kapsamında yürütülecek öğretim faaliyetleri; öğrenci katılımını desteklemeli, yaparak ve yaşayarak öğrenmeye olanak tanımalı, öğrencinin bütüncül gelişime hizmet etmelidir. *Bu çerçeve planda belirtilen okul temelli planlama haftaları örnek olarak sunulmuştur. Zümre öğretmenler kurulunda aldığınız karara göre okul ve ders koşullarınıza uygun (öğretim programında belirtilen okul temelli planlama ders saati 2 haftadan fazla sürebilir) düzenleyebilirsiniz.

EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students create a poster which is about life in 2100. They brainstorm about the possibilities in the future such as robots, aliens, space colonies, space travel, etc. Based on these ideas, students produce sentences about their future using the target grammar structures. Also, they add some visuals on their posters. The project could also be designed with the help of web 2.0 tools if students prefer. As a final stage, they present their posters in the classroom and find the common possibilities about the future. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.
EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
Expansion
Objective: To create a futuristic story about planets and space by using target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity 1: Creative Writing: Life in 2124
The teacher explains the task clearly. Students imagine life in the future, such as living on another planet. The teacher gives examples of sentences with target grammar and target vocabulary (e.g., ''If we find new planets, we will need better rockets''.). Next, students write their stories using target grammar and target vocabulary. Then, they read their stories aloud. The teacher listens and gives feedback on pronunciation and sentence correctness. Students reflect on the activity. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
Supporting
Objective: To talk about possible future scenarios in space explorations by using target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity 1: Future Space Possibilities
The teacher begins the activity by showing flashcards with key words from the word bank (e.g., robots, explore, live, discover, build) and explaining their meanings with visuals or simple definitions. Students then pair up and receive a worksheet with the target grammar such as ''If humans colonise Mars, _________________________ '', and ''If we build better rockets, ___________________________ ''. They use the word bank to fill in the blanks (e.g., ''If we build better rockets, we will explore new planets''.). In the end, the teacher provides feedback on pronunciation and accuracy. Students reflect on the activity. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.

plan.KONU:
Sub-themes: ''Planets and space; life in the universe; space explorations''
Target Vocabulary in Use (with revisional vocabulary)
Vocabulary for planets and space
Planets: Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune. Nouns: Universe, galaxy, Milky Way, solar system, satellite, a meteor, an asteroid, a comet, an orbit, to revolve, Adjective: Celestial.
Vocabulary for life in the universe
Nouns: Atmosphere, a robot, a creature, a space colony, Adjectives: tiny, unknown, weird. mysterious, rare. Vocabulary for space explorations:
Nouns: Space travel, space mission, telescope, an astronaut, a spacecraft, a rocket, a space shuttle, a space capsule Verbs: to launch, to take off, to land, to collect data, to conduct experiments, to go on a spacewalk
*National and religious days, festivals and celebrations
“29 October Republic Day”, “23 April National Sovereignty and Children’s Day”, “19 May Commemoration of Atatürk, Youth and Sports Day”, “15 July Democracy and National Unity Day”, “30 August Victory Day”, "Eid al- Fitr (Eid-al-Ramadan)", "Festival of Sacrifice (Eid-al-Adha)".
*
(Relevant language content and (communicative) activities related to these national and religious days, festivals and celebrations will be developed and integrated across all themes and in all appropriate sections wherever and whenever possible.)
*
Local Cultural, Social and Moral Considerations of the Theme
In this theme, specific examples, cases, situations, events, and practices reflecting Turkish social, cultural, and moral customs, traditions, and heritage will be included across all sub-topics. This consideration will be age-and-level appropriate and selected with the Turkish learners’ social and cultural context in mind. A table of contents for this section is provided in the introduction to the whole English Language Curriculum.
Target Grammatical Structures in Use
-
Zero Conditional: (If you go to the Moon, everything floats in space. If a planet is in orbit, it travels around a star.)
-
Conditional 1: (If you want to explore space, you can become an astronaut.)
Functions of the Target Grammatical Structures in Use
Use of the Zero Conditional: Describing general and/or scientific facts which are generally true.
Use of the Conditional 1: Describing a possible future situation.
Target Social Language Expressions in Use
It’s a small world!
She’s so strange, she is definitely not from this planet!
A star is born!
This is a whole new world!
It felt like being a man on the moon!
Target Phonological Sounds in Use
Consonants: x: (/ɛks/, /ks/, /gz/); y: (/waɪ//waɪ//waɪ/, /j/, /ɪ/, /iː/); z: /zed/ (Br), /ziː/ (AmE), /z/)
*
(Phonetic symbols will not be taught. Only sounds will be practised through the target words in the theme.)

Okul temelli planlama; zümre öğretmenler kurulu tarafından ders kapsamında gerçekleştirilmesi kararlaştırılan araştırma ve gözlem, sosyal etkinlikler, proje çalışmaları, yerel çalışmalar, okuma çalışmaları vb. çalışmaları kapsamaktadır. EK_ALANLAR.Ölçme:
PERFORMANCE ASSIGNMENT
Students create a poster which is about life in 2100. They brainstorm about the possibilities in the future such as robots, aliens, space colonies, space travel, etc. Based on these ideas, students produce sentences about their future using the target grammar structures. Also, they add some visuals on their posters. The project could also be designed with the help of web 2.0 tools if students prefer. As a final stage, they present their posters in the classroom and find the common possibilities about the future. The assignment will be evaluated by using a rubric scheme, a rating scale, and/or a marking scheme.
EK_ALANLAR.Farklılaştırma:
Expansion
Objective: To create a futuristic story about planets and space by using target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity 1: Creative Writing: Life in 2124
The teacher explains the task clearly. Students imagine life in the future, such as living on another planet. The teacher gives examples of sentences with target grammar and target vocabulary (e.g., ''If we find new planets, we will need better rockets''.). Next, students write their stories using target grammar and target vocabulary. Then, they read their stories aloud. The teacher listens and gives feedback on pronunciation and sentence correctness. Students reflect on the activity. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
Supporting
Objective: To talk about possible future scenarios in space explorations by using target vocabulary and target grammar.
Activity 1: Future Space Possibilities
The teacher begins the activity by showing flashcards with key words from the word bank (e.g., robots, explore, live, discover, build) and explaining their meanings with visuals or simple definitions. Students then pair up and receive a worksheet with the target grammar such as ''If humans colonise Mars, _________________________ '', and ''If we build better rockets, ___________________________ ''. They use the word bank to fill in the blanks (e.g., ''If we build better rockets, we will explore new planets''.). In the end, the teacher provides feedback on pronunciation and accuracy. Students reflect on the activity. Students reflect on their thoughts and feelings about the activity.
